Sports.title: NWSL team co-owned by Patrick Mahomes risks local wrath as $1.4bn project gets fresh update two years after opening
Sports.content:
The CPKC Stadium is already looking to make some upgrades, just two years after opening.

NWSL team co-owned by Patrick Mahomes risks local wrath as $1.4bn project gets fresh update two years after opening

The CPKC Stadium - home to National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) team Kansas City Current - has been handed a huge boost in funding.

The stadium, which opened in 2024, made history as it became the first ever venue that was specifically built with women's sport in mind.



3 The CPKC Stadium is hoping to undergo a redevelopment project which will see it expand to 18,000 Credit: Getty

The Current broke ground on the project back in October 2022, with the $117m cost to build the Stadium largely funded via the club's ownership.

Despite having been open for just over two years, the CPKC Stadium is hoping to undergo a revamp.

Back in May, Kansas City Mayor Quinton Lucas introduced legislation to support the expansion of the 11,500-seater stadium.



In June, the Current presented their proposal for not only the expansion of the stadium, but also some developments to the surrounding area along the Missouri River.

“For too many years, our riverfront was a landfill in the heart of our city,” Lucas said on September 10.



“Today, our riverfront is a leading destination in our region and the Midwest that’s poised to grow even more.

"With the city’s approvals, the riverfront will continue to transform into a place where people can watch a match, walk an extended trail, and be part of a vibrant neighbourhood.”



The capacity of the CPKC Stadium is set to increase to accommodate 18,000 spectators, which they will be hoping could help them attract the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup to select them as one of the host venues.

The project will also see the construction of more parking spaces, equating to 1,500 spaces, and trail connections with the aim of making it the "most innovative public-private sports and entertainment project in the Midwest."

Furthermore, with the addition of shops around the area, the project seeks to cement Kansas City's riverfront as its premier sports and entertainment for women's sports.

3 Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany co-own the Current Credit: Getty



3 The Current's stadium is the first ever made specifically for women's sports Credit: Getty

With the support of Lucas' proposal, the expansion and redevelopment is estimated to become a $1.4 billion project.

The KCMO is set to pitch in an estimated $185 million, funded through sales tax revenue generated by the current stadium and surrounding district.

According to KSHB 41, the debt shortfalls will become the responsibility of the Current's ownership group, which includes NFL superstar Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany, so taxpayers avoid any harm.



Mixed views on going ahead with the redevelopment project

Council member Wes Rogers from the 2nd District compared the proposed riverfront transformation to the past revival of downtown Kansas City in the early 2000's.

“There was just nothing there,” Rogers said recalling what the area was like back in 1998. “There were no businesses; there were no people living down there. And what we’ve done the past 25 years is pretty spectacular, and it has grown our economy.”

“It has made us a bigger, better city; a more vibrant city; a city with a bigger tax base.

"And when we do big projects like this the right way — and I believe this one is, particularly because of the Current backing — I am happy to vote yes and celebrate.”



However, the project has also met some pushback from vocal critics, who have also criticised other projects in the state, including the plans for the MLB team Royals' new ballpark at Crown Center, suggesting that approving these projects are fiscally irresponsible.

“We are making a decision to essentially take a gamble and bet on these projects, when I don’t think we need to do all the time,” council member Jonathan Duncan, 6th District, said.

“It’s incumbent upon this body to consider that even if these bonds are backed by another entity, this isn’t free money.

"We are retracting revenue that would be going to our general fund and back into projects. We are doing it again and again and again.”



“At some point, we’re going to have to ask: ‘When are we going to start prioritizing our general fund?’” he continued.

“I really feel like we are not taking a full accounting of how much revenue we are redirecting into projects that we won’t see a return on in 30 years.”

Sports.title: EFL legend Ross McCormack signs for tier 9 club aged 40 in surprise announcement
Sports.content:
EFL legend Ross McCormack signs for tier 9 club aged 40 in surprise announcement

Add us as preferred source

Ross McCormack has returned to English football by joining a club in the ninth-tier.

The former Scotland striker has joined Knaresborough Town of the Northern Counties East Football League Premier Division.

3 McCormack has joined Knaresborough Town in the ninth-tier of English football Credit: Getty Images - Getty

His arrival at the North Yorkshire-based outfit comes just a month after McCormack signed for Scottish amateur side Giffnock North.

He had previously been without a club for almost two-and-a-half years after leaving Doncaster City in March 2024.

McCormack previously had spells in Scotland, England and Australia before dropping into non-league.

Knaresborough have now become the 15th club of his football career.

The Boro announced the signing of McCormack on Tuesday ahead of a Northern Counties East Football League Cup tie against Penistone Church.

While Knaresborough went on to win 2-0, McCormack was not involved.

He could instead make his debut at home to Horbury Town on Saturday at the 1,000-capacity Manse Lane.

Knaresborough currently sit seventh in the table after seven matches this season.

McCormack's career to date

McCormack has been playing non-league football since 2020 following a 17-year professional career.

Having left Aston Villa in the summer of 2019, he joined Aldershot in the National League 14 months later.

3 McCormack's career has included spells in Scotland, England and Australia Credit: Getty

Spells have since followed at Liversedge and Doncaster City as well as making his boxing debut in April of this year.

McCormack started his senior career with Rangers, winning a Scottish Premiership title in 2005.

After a loan spell with Doncaster Rovers, he moved to Motherwell in 2006 before joining Cardiff City two years later.

The forward would then go on to score 120 goals in 333 Championship appearances for Cardiff, Leeds United, Fulham, Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest.

His tally includes a 28-goal haul to win the golden boot with Leeds in the 2013/14 season.

McCormack is also the fourth-highest scorer in Championship history behind Billy Sharp, Jordan Rhodes and David Nugent.

3 McCormack is the fourth-highest scorer in Championship history Credit: Getty

However, he made the fewest appearances in the division out of the top four.

During his time at Villa, McCormack also had loan spells with Melbourne City, Central Coast Mariners and Motherwell.

At international level, he was handed his senior Scotland debut by George Burley as a 21-year-old in 2008.

McCormack went on to score twice in 13 caps for his country, with the last of those appearances coming against Italy in 2016.

Sports.title: Ange Postecoglou in heated exchange with journalist over Cristiano Ronaldo
Sports.content:
Saudi football journalists are learning very quickly that it's not a wise idea to poke the bear that is Ange Postecoglou.

After Postecoglou's Al Nassr were beaten 4-0 by Al Ain in their AFC Champions League Elite opener, one local reporter decided to aim a string of criticisms towards the Australian.



3 Al Nassr's loss to Al Ain was their second defeat in the last four games Credit: Getty

The reporter questioned the club's pre-season preparations in Portugal, prompting Postecoglou to ask if the former was there.

After the reporter confirmed his attendance, Postecoglou said: "And what happened? No, no, but you need to explain because you say we didn't prepare well, but you were there. You're not saying the truth. Be honest.

"It's my responsibility. Maybe I haven't done my job well, but please don't talk about preparation because in Portugal, how many of these players were in Portugal?"



The reporter replied: "But they came ready from national teams."

A stunned Postecoglou said: "Oh, they came ready. Okay."

What did the Saudi reporter say about Cristiano Ronaldo?

The same reporter then turned his attention to Al Nassr superstar Cristiano Ronaldo, claiming the Portuguese icon's 'presence does not benefit the team, especially in matches'.

Postecoglou quickly reminded the reporter Ronaldo has scored three times already despite having a 'limited preparation' as he was away with Portugal at the World Cup.



The Al Nassr boss continued: "This is not about the players. They are top players and they have great character. The responsibility is mine.

"It's me, but you shouldn't say that about somebody who is still setting an example for everyone.



"And you should be careful when you say things like that about people who have built a career on making all the sacrifices to keep playing.

3 Ronaldo has started six of his seven appearances for Al Nassr this term Credit: Getty

"You can criticise me, no problem. That's okay, but you need to be careful."

Postecoglou then asked the reporter if Ronaldo had not scored in three games and didn't have chances against Al Ain, to which they replied: "The last three matches, he did nothing."



The former Tottenham boss clapped back: "He did nothing? Well, you're watching a different game to me."

Al Nassr's brutal fixture run

Tuesday's defeat to Al Ain was Al Nassr's ninth fixture in the space of a month and fourth in the space of 10 days.

Despite the congested schedule, Postecoglou conceded the result was a 'disappointing one.'

“It was always going to be a difficult game with the schedule we’ve had but the first goal we conceded, it made the task more difficult," Postecoglou said.



3 Postecoglou will have to weather a fixture storm yet again in the not-too-distant future Credit: Getty

“The players still stuck to it and tried as hard as they could, but we couldn’t get a goal back in he game and then obviously we had to open up to try and score, and Al Ain took advantage.”

Postecoglou and his Al Nassr troops will now have almost a month off before they return to action due to the international break.

But once competition resumes, there will be no slowing down for Postecoglou's side.



As it stands, Al Nassr will play four matches in the space of nine days, beginning with a clash against Diriyah on October 9.

Sports.title: Unanimous Gabriel red card verdict delivered by Premier League panel after Emi Martinez head kick
Sports.content:
Arsenal defender Gabriel officially does not need to consider himself lucky.

Gabriel ran the risk of a red card when his boot connected with goalkeeper Emi Martinez's face in the early stages of Arsenal's 2-1 win over Chelsea on September 6.



2 The Brazilian's challenge ignited Chelsea's fury

Martinez required medical treatment following the challenge but Gabriel escaped punishment from referee Chris Kavanagh and following a VAR check.

What was the Key Match Incident panel's official verdict?

The Key Match Incident panel has now backed up the verdict from the match, with all five members voting that it was the correct call.

"The panel unanimously supported the referee's call of no red card," the panel commentary said.



"Multiple players were on the ground competing and challenging for the loose ball, and the action of Gabriel was not deemed to be an act of violent conduct or serious foul play."

What is Gabriel's disciplinary record with Arsenal?

Had Gabriel been sent off, it would have been the first time he'd been shown a straight red card for Arsenal.



The Brazilian has previously been given his marching orders twice for the Gunners in 265 appearancs for the club.

He has also been shown 32 yellow cards following his arrival from Lille in 2020.



Both of his dismissals came as second yellows cards after earlier being cautioned.

How Arsenal's win over Chelsea unfolded

Gabriel's mistimed challenge on Martinez came just minutes after Morgan Rogers handed Chelsea an early lead at the Emirates Stadium.

But Chelsea weren't even ahead for a whole half as Kai Havertz struck before the interval to level the score.

2 Odegaard's winner against Chelsea was his second league goal this season Credit: AFP



Gunners skipper Martin Odegaard completed the comeback in the second half, handing Chelsea their only Premier League defeat this term.

Although Gabriel got off scot-free with his incident against Chelsea, his central defensive partner Ezri Konsa had no such luck during Arsenal's win over Sunderland last Saturday.

Konsa, who joined Arsenal this summer from Aston Villa, was adjudged to have hauled down Black Cats defender Dan Ballard to the ground while Kevin Danso's long throw got hurled into the box.

Luckily for Konsa, he was bailed out by Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya who perfectly read where Sunderland's Enzo Le Fee would direct his spot kick.



However, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was left furious that a penalty was even awared in the first place.

"I think everybody can see it [is not a foul] and it's not acceptable at this level and I'm very, very worried," Arteta told talkSPORT following the match.

Arteta continued: "It's not soft, it's a judo roll, what he does on our player is never a penalty from every angle, I watched it ten times.

"That's why we have all the cameras and this cannot happen, it changes the momentum of the season, the course of the championship at this level, it cannot happen."

Sports.title: Manchester United warned JJ Gabriel decision will cost them future transfers
Sports.content:
Ally McCoist believes JJ Gabriel's decision to seek a move away from Manchester United will have an alarming domino effect.

Gabriel, 15, sparked headlines on Tuesday when it emerged he asked to leave the Red Devils.

3 Gabriel recently scored a hat-trick in his UEFA Youth League debut Credit: Getty

What is the latest on JJ Gabriel's future?

talkSPORT understands Real Madrid are now leading the race for the teen sensation's signature but face competition from Barcelona and two Premier League clubs.

Despite Gabriel's desire for a new challenge, the Red Devils remain hopeful of rectifying the situation.

Should Gabriel depart, it would deprive United of yet another top English talent.

The Red Devils have historically been synonymous with producing elite homegrown players and also prising them away from other clubs.

But that trend has slowly regressed in recent years, with the likes of Elliot Anderson, Morgan Rogers and Declan Rice all spurning United's advances over the years.

Ally McCoist reacts to JJ Gabriel's exit demand

It's why McCoist fears the Red Devils losing Gabriel could have long-term ramifications in the transfer market.

"The fact of the matter is, top players in world football now will choose other clubs before Manchester United because they've got a better chance of winning," McCoist said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

Over the last nine seasons, the Red Devils have won just two major trophies.

Additionally, United have finished in the top four of the Premier League only six times since they last won the competition, which was in 2013.

All signs point to a club that is far removed from its glory days.

3 Anderson had been on United's wish list but opted to join Manchester City in a £116m deal Credit: Getty

It was hoped that Gabriel, who has been dubbed the 'kid Messi', would eventually play a significant role in reversing United's malaise of late.

But those aspirations now appear to be dashed, with Gabriel's father, a former Republic of Ireland international, believed to be playing a driving role in the controversy.

Alex Crook's verdict on the latest JJ Gabriel developments

McCoist's fears about how damaging Gabriel's exit could be to United's future transfer dealings was echoed by talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook.

"I think optically it's a really bad look if Manchester United lose somebody who Ryan Giggs has gone on record as saying he's a generational talent," Crook said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"Particularly if he was to join another English club, it probably tells you where United are at in terms of pulling power."

Gabriel was due to be named in United's matchday squad for their Carabao Cup third round clash against Brighton on Wednesday evening, live on talkSPORT.

3 Gabriel netted 23 times in 23 U18 Premier League fixtures last term Credit: Getty

But the latest developments have plunged his potential inclusion into doubt.

Should Gabriel take the field, he will become United's youngest-ever player.

Goalkeeper David Gaskell is the incumbent record holder after he played his first game aged 16 years and 19 days.

Sports.title: Two Arsenal players sent warning as Max Dowman labelled better than Cesc Fabregas and Jack Wilshere at 16
Sports.content:
Two Arsenal players sent warning as Max Dowman labelled better than Cesc Fabregas and Jack Wilshere at 16

Arsenal starlet Max Dowman is hot on the heels of Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze - he's a generational talent.

That's the view of fellow Hale End graduate Adrian Clarke, who has waxed lyrical over the 16-year-old following his man of the match display against Ipswich.



4 Dowman broke the deadlock away at Ipswich as Arsenal eased to victory in their third round Carabao Cup tie Credit: Getty

The teenager banged in a classy double in Tuesday night's 4-2 win at Portman Road to help send the Gunners into the Carabao Cup fourth round.

In doing so, Dowman became just the second 16-year-old after Wayne Rooney to bag a brace for a Premier League side in any competition.

It was the versatile attacking midfielder's first outing of the season having enjoyed a historic 2025/26 campaign, in which he scored once in 13 matches.



And for Clarke, who featured in nine first-team fixtures for Arsenal in the 1990s, he believes Dowman is a better talent at 16 than Cesc Fabregas and Jack Wilshere were at the same age for the north Londoners.

Fabregas and Wilshere both made their debuts at 16 - a year older than Dowman did - before fully breaking into the starting XI under Arsene Wenger at 17 and 18 respectively.



What has Adrian Clarke said about Max Dowman?

Speaking on the Sports Breakfast show, Clarke was asked about Dowman's mercurial talent, which has him knocking on Mikel Arteta's door.

To which he said: "What about that [first] goal? The way that he sort of skipped around [Cedric] Kipre, it's the sort of goal that ordinary players don't score.



"It's as simple as that, it was a little bit special in terms of his balance and the way that he skipped around him, it was amazing, but it wasn't just that.

"The second goal, the ball comes off someone's hand, he takes it with the outside of his foot, another little touch, then he passes it in the far corner.

"He's very, very calm, I haven't seen a 16-year-old as good as Max Dowman, I just haven't.

4 Dowman's second strike at Portman Road saw him join an exclusive club alongside Rooney Credit: AFP



"And I've been privileged to watch players like Jack Wilshere come through very early, Cesc Fabregas as well, who were both brilliant."

Clarke continued: "I think he's got the right manager, I think Mikel Arteta is pretty sensible, I think he's aware of the bigger picture.

"Look, it's never been harder for a young player to get close to the Arsenal first team, a lot of players get their chance when the team's struggling, this team is the opposite of struggling, it's so strong from back to front.

"And there are so many amazing players in Max's position, but he's there on merit, he's not there because, 'Oh, he's a good prospect, we want to give him some experience.'



"He's there because he's good enough to make a difference among all those great players right now, he's a phenomenon, there's no doubt about it, but they have to look after him."

And Clarke also believes that skipper Odegaard and Eze should be looking over their shoulder regarding Dowman, with the youngster impressing whenever he's given a chance.

4 Both Fabregas and Wilshere came through Arsenal's academy, where they went on to become cult heroes Credit: Getty

The 51-year-old remarked: "He's got the immediate respect of the players, I must have watched every appearance he's made for the first time, I think 13 last year, a few pre-season games.



"The one thing that stood out right from the first time I saw him was that the senior players couldn't give him enough of the ball, there was no, 'Oh yeah, look at him, nah, I'll go to someone else.'

"It was like, 'Nah, let's give it to Max, he'll make something happen,' this boy is definitely special, he got to play last night in his preferred position, which definitely is a No.10.

"He's not getting in ahead of Martin Odegaard at the moment, not the form he's in, with Eze there, it's not easy either.

"If he gets a run of games at some point in the No.10 position for Arsenal, he will deliver, I've got no doubt about it."



What history has Max Dowman made at Arsenal?

Dowman, who was incredibly told by Adrian Durham last season to depart the club for the sake of his career, is the youngest player to get his hands on the Premier League trophy.

4 Hale End graduate Dowman is regarded as one of the best talents in world football Credit: Getty

He also holds the record as being the youngest goalscorer in competition, along with being the youngest to ever start a Premier League game.

While he is also the youngest to feature in a Champions League match - doing so aged 15 and 308 days old.



Dowman will now be hoping to make his first top-fight outing this term away at Brighton on Saturday having been left out of the matchday squad in two of Arsenal's last three games.

Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara wishes Tottenham got relegated and storms out of studio after argument with Jason Cundy boils over
Sports.content:
Jamie O’Hara wishes Tottenham got relegated and storms out of studio after argument with Jason Cundy boils over

Jamie O’Hara took his Tottenham frustration to new heights by claiming the club should have been relegated last season.

The Sports Bar host endured yet another sombre start to the show on Tuesday night following his beloved Spurs’ Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool.



7 It was another match without victory for Roberto De Zerbi's Spurs Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

7 O'Hara cut a dejected figure on Tuesday's Sports Bar

Roberto De Zerbi’s side were beaten 3-1 at a rain-soaked Anfield to bring about an early end to any hopes of winning the competition.

Goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai were enough to sweep Spurs aside who had pulled one back late on through Conor Gallagher.



The midfielder’s close range finish was Tottenham’s first goal anywhere this season after drawing blanks in their opening four league games.

And with a season that is already mirroring those of the previous two campaigns, O’Hara, who later in the show stormed out of the talkSPORT studio, appeared to have already reached his limit.



O'Hara's passionate tirade

“Seriously, what is going on?,” O’Hara said opening up Tuesday’s show.

“I feel like everyday I wake up and it’s the same thing.

“Every single time Spurs play, I look at the fixtures and I'm like, ‘Spurs are playing tonight, alright, here we go, get beat.’



“I don’t know what to say. It’s groundhog day.

Things were made doubly worse for the ex-Spurs midfielder with partner-in-crime Jason Cundy lapping up every second of his co-host’s misery.

“This is the perfect night again for Cundy. When is my night?” O’Hara ranted.

7 Dominik Szoboszlai's superb effort from range was the pick of the goals at Anfield Credit: Getty

“I’ve been here for five years and I’ve had one good night. One. The Europa League final, that was it.



“It’s absolute guff, it really is and I’m sick and tired of it. I know it’s all great and everyone enjoys it but this is actually getting ridiculous.

“Where do Spurs go from here? We have got a disease. We don’t know how to win. Even when we score we get beat,

“Every single game no matter what, Spurs get beat. Spend £400million – get beat.

“Score – get beat. New manager – get beat.

“We’ve got a disease."

7 Cundy did his best to further wind up his co-host - and succeeded



Cundy then hilariously chimed in describing the disease as an incurable one.

Just when listeners thought O’Hara had got everything off his chest, he made the bold suggestion that Tottenham should have been relegated last season.

Championship level

“You know what should have happened, we should have gone down. We are so bad,” he added.

“We’re shocking. The only reason we stayed up is because Aston Villa guffed it and Everton jacked it in at the end of the season.



“I thought, we might start the new season and see something different, something positive.

“No, absolute guff again. We don’t deserve to be playing Premier League teams. We are absolutely useless.”

7 Conor Gallagher's late goal, which reduced Spurs' deficit from 2-0 to 2-1, was the only highlight of the night for Spurs Credit: Getty

O’Hara then bravely asked his co-host to provide him with one positive from Tuesday’s cup tie to which Cundy cheekily replied: “You scored tonight at a Premier League ground. First time that’s happened this season.”



And that set O’Hara off on yet another rant.

“The problem is we don’t take our chances and are soft,” he said. “Ice creams. We’re like a flake in 30 degree heat.

“And why is [Mathys] Tel still playing? I'd rather Richarlison played.

“He’s guff, he’s terrible, he’s got trampoline feet. He’s everything that’s bad about Tottenham. We signed him for £50m.”

O'Hara storms out of studio

After over an hour of being tormented by talkSPORT's chief wind-up merchant Cundy, it all got a bit much for O'Hara.



7 O'Hara simply couldn't take Cundy's ribbing any longer

7 O'Hara needed some air for a few minutes before returning to hosting duties for the second half of the show

The 39-year-old made for a sharp exit mid-show after arguing with Cundy about Mathys Tel's use to the Spurs team.

O'Hara questioned why De Zerbi continues to select the French winger, even suggesting replacing Tel with the exiled Richarlison would be a better option for Spurs.



Cundy launched a defence, albeit a sarcastic one, of Tel's value to the team - and O'Hara decided enough was enough.

After the break, O'Hara returned to his hosting duties for more ribbing by his mate.

Sports.title: JIMMY MONTGOMERY EXCLUSIVE: Sunderland's FA Cup hero on the hijinks of the Black Cats' last European adventure, having his gloves stolen in Lisbon - and his verdict on Robin Roefs
Sports.content:
In the hall of Jimmy Montgomery’s peaceful house in the Sunderland suburbs is a framed black-and-white photograph of the save in the 1973 FA Cup final for which he will forever be remembered.

It’s a simple picture, an iconic moment beautifully captured.

The players of Sunderland and Leeds are in classic football strips, free of clutter and sponsors' logos. Long hair and black boots. Meanwhile a goalkeeper dives low into history to parry a header wearing a pair of woollen gloves that look like they could have come from a local garden centre.

‘I haven’t got those gloves anymore,’ Montgomery tells the Daily Mail from his seat on the sofa.

‘When we played in Lisbon (against Sporting) in the Cup Winners' Cup the next season, I put them in the back of the net with my cap as I always did. And somebody stole them.

‘Ball boy? Cameraman? I have no idea. So that was one souvenir gone in a flash.

‘Not that it really mattered. I hardly wore them. When they were wet they were about as much use as a chocolate watch!’

Sunderland legend Jimmy Montgomery has fond memories of the club's last European campaign in 1973-74 - apart from having his goalkeeper gloves stolen in Lisbon!

Montgomery has a framed photo of the save in the 1973 FA Cup final against Leeds for which he will forever be remembered

We are here on Wearside to talk, for once, not about that stunning double save that helped second-tier Sunderland win the Cup at Wembley 53 years ago, but about the European campaign that followed.

It was the club’s first foray into Europe and, until today, their last.

As Regis Le Bris’ impressive modern team face AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League tomorrow night, Montgomery will be in the stand that, since the start of last season, carries his name.

‘We played our first tie in Budapest behind the Iron Curtain and it was the exact same XI that had won the cup final,’ recalls Montgomery. ‘I don’t think that was sentiment. I think we deserved it.

‘These days the team will have a dossier on the opponents and take their own chef and staff with them.

‘We had our manager Bob Stokoe, his assistant and maybe the club secretary. That was it.

‘In terms of the opposition (Vasas Budapest) we didn’t know a thing about them apart from what the press men on the plane told us.

‘It took us for ever to get there and even longer to get back. But we won 2-0 and also beat them at home. Marvellous.

‘It ended for us in the next round at Sporting Lisbon. That was a strange night.

‘They had ball-boys throwing the balls on but when they did, the Lisbon players would throw them straight off again, sometimes straight into the crowd.

‘We looked at the ref and he just stared back at us. I guess it was time-wasting. But I have never seen anything like it before or since.’

Sunderland captain Bobby Kerr is held aloft by his team-mates, including Montgomery (fourth from right) after the 1-0 win over Leeds in 1973

Now, at the age of 82, Montgomery is revered to such a degree he literally has his name written throughout the modern Sunderland

Facing a shot from Newcastle's Jim Scott in the Tyne-Wear derby at Roker Park in 1968

Montgomery made a record 627 appearances for his hometown club across 18 years. As a boy he would watch his team at Roker Park with his father. As an apprentice, he would later sweep the terraces and paint the seats.

Now, at the age of 82, he is revered to such a degree he literally has his name written throughout the modern Sunderland.

As well as the stand at the Stadium of Light, this year’s goalkeeping jerseys have his signature, number of appearances and even an outline of his famous save embossed in them.

‘It’s hard to believe,' he says. ‘I am just a kid from down the road.’

Montgomery has served Sunderland as player, goalkeeping coach and worked at its centre of excellence.

‘I have actually been let go four times and that was hard,’ he says. ‘Different managers would want different things. So yeah I got kicked out.

‘But I kept getting invited back again!

‘I even had a year coaching at Newcastle with Kevin Keegan and, as hard as it is for Sunderland fans to hear, Pavel Srnicek was perhaps the best I worked with.’

A welcome visitor to Sunderland’s training ground whenever his health allows, Montgomery has talked football with the ever-respectful Le Bris and goalkeeping with current No 1 Robin Roefs.

‘They sometimes bring the goalkeepers over for a chat,’ he explains. ‘I think the young ones want to talk. That’s very humbling and typical of the club now.

Montgomery made a record 627 appearances for his hometown club across 18 years

Montgomery (second left) poses with the Cup alongside (from left) Ian Porterfield, Micky Horswill and Kerr

‘Robin is an excellent keeper, a brilliant keeper. Sometimes I just wish he wouldn't try to play from the back so much. I'm not a great fan of it. I get wound up.

‘It’s a risk. I would much rather goalkeepers get it forward, push the team up, and start from there.

‘I'm a big believer in once the goalkeeper's got the ball, he's in charge of it. He does what he thinks right.

‘If he doesn't want to play it short, he shouldn't have to. Look at the Arsenal goalkeeper on Saturday. He dictated everything. He was fully in charge. I like that.’

If Montgomery was impressed with David Raya, he was less enamoured with Arsenal.

‘I have no time for them,’ he says. ‘Goodness I couldn’t watch that every week. What is that type of football?

‘Their manager is complaining like mad about giving the penalty away but if you're going to get mixed up in that, it will go against you eventually.

‘It’s amazing what goes on at corners now. They don’t even look at the ball. We never grappled like that. I just knew that when the ball came over I was gonna get smashed.

‘Wyn Davies of Newcastle and good old Nat Lofthouse. Every time. Bang. There was no protection. You just had to be ready for it.’

At the end of his career, Montgomery spent a season at Nottingham Forest under Brian Clough.

‘I played with Brian and he was brilliant, though he knew it too,’ he smiles. ‘I was playing the day he broke his leg on Boxing Day in 1962. So I was chuffed he thought I was good enough all those years later to be under-study to Shilts (Peter Shilton).

‘I was in my mid-30s and coming towards the end. I never played but was on the bench when Forest won the European Cup in Madrid in 1980. I got a medal.’

Montgomery – who rates the great Pat Jennings as perhaps the best goalkeeper he has known – has a photo of himself with the European Cup and it feels strange to see him in another club’s colours.

‘I have no time for them,’ says Montgomery of Arsenal. ‘Goodness I couldn’t watch that every week. What is that type of football?

But it’s that black-and-white picture of his Wembley save that we return to.

The first effort – the one on the picture – was from Trevor Cherry. The follow-up from five yards from Peter Lorimer was struck so powerfully ITV commentator Brian Moore shouted ‘goal’ before it struck the underside of the bar.

Afterwards, it was the late Jimmy Hill who declared it had been the tips of Montgomery’s fingers that had touched it up on to the woodwork.

Montgomery’s favourite line is to say he wished he had caught the first shot so he wouldn’t have had to spend his life talking about the second.

‘But I don’t mean it,’ he smiles. ‘I love what it still means to people.

‘It was only when standing with my pint of milk afterwards that I realised the significance of it. They just kept showing it.

‘I was lucky it was on TV, mind. I had made one from a lad playing for Hull a few weeks before that was even better…’

Sports.title: 'He can become one of the ultimate legends of the game': England bowling guru TROY COOLEY on what he loves about his attack, how Jofra Archer is still improving, why Josh Tongue is 'unique' and the other bowlers on his Ashes radar
Sports.content:
'He can become one of the ultimate legends of the game': England bowling guru TROY COOLEY on what he loves about his attack, how Jofra Archer is still improving, why Josh Tongue is 'unique' and the other bowlers on his Ashes radar

It’s not hard to see why Troy Cooley – world cricket’s fast-bowling whisperer – gets on so well with his charges, easy to grasp why England were so keen to lure him back after 20 years away.

Ask him anything about his trade and he responds with a laugh and a quip, followed by an answer that is both engaging and engaged. He’s a people person, a believer in the art of his job as well as the science. He got the best out of England’s famous 2005 Ashes pace quartet, and is now trying to contain his excitement about Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson.

And, armed with a dislike of batsmen that is both hammed-up and genuine, he has no doubt which of cricket’s two main skills is the tougher.

‘Batters get a stress fracture of the brain when they do too much,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport while on manoeuvres at Grace Road, where he is keeping an eye on the quicks of Leicestershire and Hampshire. ‘Bowlers get a stress fracture of the body.’

Cooley is 60, having stayed close to the peak of the game since his three-year stint with Duncan Fletcher’s England side ended in 2006 – between their 2–1 Ashes win of 2005 inspired by Steve Harmison, Matthew Hoggard, Andrew Flintoff and Simon Jones, and their harrowing 5–0 Ashes whitewash in 2006-07.

By then, the Tasmanian-born Cooley had become bowling coach of his native Australia, and it was tempting to note that he had a curious habit of helping the victors. Now, after long spells in Australia and India, he was re-signed by the ECB in January, and intends to be on the winning side once more when the Ashes battle resumes next summer.

England's fast bowling coach Troy Cooley, 60, is impressed with England's current attack of Gus Atkinson, Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue

Robinson, who averaged 8.76 against Pakistan, can transfer his skills overseas, insists Cooley

To hear him talk about the current fast-bowling foursome, who knocked over Pakistan for five successive scores below 200 before being belted over all Edgbaston by tailender Razaullah, is to believe it’s perfectly possible.

Asked whether he thinks Archer, who touched 94mph this summer, can get better, he replies: ‘Of course he can. He’s had a history of trying to get himself on the park, and he’s learned how his body adapts and works. He’s got the mentality that he wants to get better.

‘He’s got the skill level to become one of the ultimate legends of the game, one of those great champions everyone talks about.’

He believes that Robinson, who averaged 8.76 against Pakistan, can transfer his skills overseas, and raves about his control.

‘Out… stand… ding,’ he says, breaking the word into its syllables. ‘He’s tall. He’s got bounce. He moves the ball, so he misses the middle of the bat on most occasions –left and right, up and down.

‘One of the key things I say to our bowlers is all we’ve got to do is miss the middle of the bat. Then the batter gets frustrated and he’s going to make a stupid mistake. We lay the beautiful trap.’

As much as anything, Cooley is excited by variety. Where Harmison offered bounce, Hoggard swing, Flintoff pace and Jones reverse-swing, the current crop all have their USPs too – not least Tongue, with an action that goes beyond the perpendicular, luring right-handers into playing at deliveries better left alone.

Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson bring unique skills to the England attack

And Jofra Archer, says Cooley, 'can become one of the ultimate legends of the game'

‘He’s unique, and that’s what we’re after,’ Cooley says of Tongue. ‘But he doesn’t just release the ball from a different position: he bowls at bloody 90mph, and for most batters decision-making starts to get interrupted at about 85.’

Only Atkinson failed to help himself to wickets against Pakistan, and while Cooley insists he adds ‘an integral glue to this group’, citing his ‘great arm speed, ability to move the ball and sharp bouncer’, he also admits: ‘He’s just got to work out which bowler he wants to be.’

He adds: ‘I like the fact that he’s dogged. He’s just got to stay fit, which was one of his big issues before: we’d play a couple of games and then he’d be down on pace and his hamstring is hanging off. But he’ll be OK.’

So what about that third evening in Birmingham, when England’s quicks were battered into submission by Razaullah’s nine sixes, and Joe Root rushed off the field, presumably for dressing-room advice?

‘I just thought that maybe they needed a bit of consolidation around what we’re going to do here,’ Cooley says. ‘Remember, our best ball has got the top order out so far. Let’s just hang in there a bit longer, let’s not try and finish this too early. When you get a bit emotional, the process goes out the window sometimes.

‘I think the captain and the rest of the team will learn from that. But there’s nothing like denting a bit of pride to get someone out of their comfort zone.’

Cooley points to the strength in depth of English fast bowling, and mentions Sussex seamer Henry Crocombe, as well as three others who have played Test cricket over the last two summers: Sam Cook, Matt Fisher and Sonny Baker, who on Tuesday night spoke about his winter touring ambitions after taking three for 12 in England’s T20 demolition of Sri Lanka in Southampton.

Cooley believes that Atkinson 'has just got to work out which bowler he wants to be’

Cooley helped England win the 2005 Ashes and would like to repeat the trick next year

Above all, he wants to create a fast-bowling unit that can perform abroad as well as it can at home – what he calls the ‘holy grail’ of his job. And, as ever, his tendency is to seek the clearest, simplest explanation.

‘I mean, it is still about hitting the top of off and taking responsibility that my job is to take a wicket, stop runs and stay fit to perform. And I’m going to be able to do that anywhere I rock up, because I have worked hard enough on the skills.’

Cooley laughs, but the message is deadly serious. England have the right man in place for a crack at Australia.

Sports.title: Football legend Ronald Koeman announces death of wife, 65, following breast cancer battle in heartbreaking tribute after 41-year marriage
Sports.content:
Football legend Ronald Koeman announces death of wife, 65, following breast cancer battle in heartbreaking tribute after 41-year marriage

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Football legend Ronald Koeman has announced the death of his beloved wife Bartina from breast cancer aged 65.

The former Netherlands and Barcelona boss and his other half were married for 41 years and he shared a heartbreaking message with the news on Instagram.

Koeman, 63, wrote: 'With intense sadness, but also with great pride and love, we say goodbye to my beautiful wife, our dearest mom and grandma.'

The image he shared to accompany the post was a black and white shot of the couple looking into each other's eyes and clasping their hands together.

Koeman, who established himself as a football legend during his decorated playing career for Barcelona, Ajax, PSV and Feyenoord, married Bartina back in 1985.

They had three children and four grandchildren together during a long and happy marriage.

Ronald Koeman posted this image of him and his late wife Bartina, announcing her death

Koeman, pictured with Bartina and his children in 1997 after a Feyenoord game, was married to Bartina for 41 years

Bartina was re-diagnosed with breast cancer in 2023 when he started his second spell in charge of the Dutch national team.

She had previously recovered from breast cancer in 2010 and it came back in 2018.

Bartina continued to fight the disease and Koeman said metastases had been detected last year, which his wife was receiving treatment for.

When he stepped down from the Dutch job, he made a point of thanking his wife for her support, saying: 'My wife Bartina supported and encouraged me every day, despite her own illness, to finish my work as national coach.

'That is a testament to incredible strength. I am more grateful to her for that than I will ever be able to put into words.'

Bartina thrived in her own successful career as an entrepreneur and had her own cosmetics and skincare line.

And Koeman has received an outpouring of support, with tributes flooding in on social media following the announcement.

The couple share a laugh in 2022 during a match between Telstar and Helmond Sport

Legendary goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar wrote: 'My deepest condolences and wishing you all much strength together as a family.'

Denzel Dumfries, Brian Brobbey, Ryan Gravenberch, Nathan Ake and a number of other Dutch stars who played under Koeman replied to his message with a heart emoji.

Koeman, who managed Southampton and Everton in the Premier League, has not taken another job since stepping down from the Netherlands job after their World Cup elimination by Morocco in the round of 32.

Sports.title: EFL manager explains decision to substitute star striker after just 44 SECONDS of match in bid to bypass competition rules
Sports.content:
EFL manager explains decision to substitute star striker after just 44 SECONDS of match in bid to bypass competition rules

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

York City manager Scott Lindsey has called the rule that led him to make a substitute after 44 seconds 'massively ridiculous'.

Lindsey remarkably substituted star striker Ollie Pearce less than a minute into the League Two side's 3-1 defeat to Newcastle U21s in the EFL Trophy, with Ben Farrar coming on for his senior debut in his place.

'Massively ridiculous,' Lindsey said. 'Ollie's trained today; the boys that are in the first team played against the youth team. And then he had to come tonight and do that; it's ridiculous. But we had to do it because we have to tick all the boxes for the rules.'

The EFL Trophy laws state that all EFL clubs 'must include' at least four senior members of their squad in the starting line-up, otherwise known as 'Qualifying Players'.

In the competition handbook, a qualifying player is described as somebody who had started the immediately preceding first team game, has made 40 or more first team starting appearances, or is on standard loan from a Premier League Club or any EFL Club operating a Category One Academy.

The rule led to Lindsey having to start four of his senior stars, including Pearce, who has scored 67 goals in 102 appearances for the club.

York City's Ollie Pearce was substituted after 44 seconds against Newcastle U21s on Tuesday

He continued: 'It's madness, it really is, it's ludicrous. And I think it's actually stopping younger players for clubs like ourselves playing. Ben Farrar is starting on the bench, but he should be starting that game.

'I think they try and support Premier League clubs rather than clubs at our level. They want the Premier League clubs to play against seasoned pros, which is fine. But then it doesn't help our homegrown talent.

'They have to look at the rules for this competition, definitely.'

Pearce bagged a goal and an assist in York's 4-0 thumping of Swindon Town at the weekend, and was most likely hoping to be in the stands against the Newcastle U21s, earning a rest.

The only thing that stopped the striker doing that for the entire game was the location of his house.

'The reason that I picked Ollie Pearce is because he lives in York,' Lindsey continued. 'I'm not even joking. I didn't want anybody travelling from Sheffield or wherever they lived to play for 30 seconds. It would have been a waste of time.

'I said to him afterward it's the best he's played, we had a bit of banter about that. He said to me, "if I get a penalty in the first 30 seconds, can I take it?" And I said no, the board will be coming up.'

Sports.title: 'Where's OUR apology?': Enzo Maresca claims Man City have waited THREE years for call from referees' boss Howard Webb as he hits back at Erling Haaland row
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca declared that Manchester City are still waiting on an apology from referees’ chief Howard Webb for a controversial derby goal in 2023.

The weekend victory at Old Trafford was enveloped by controversy, Pro Ref admitting a mistake by the VAR officials for awarding Erling Haaland’s 60th-minute goal despite Enzo Fernandez interfering with play in an offside position.

Webb was in contact with Manchester United in the immediate aftermath, with VAR Matt Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus stood down for the coming week’s Premier League matches.

Maresca questioned why that process was different to the one City experienced when he was Pep Guardiola’s assistant in City’s Treble campaign.

Bruno Fernandes had equalised for United at Old Trafford in January 2023 despite Marcus Rashford seemingly interfering with play while stood offside. A discombobulated City then conceded another to Rashford minutes later.

Enzo Maresca questioned why that process was different to the one City experienced when he was Pep Guardiola’s assistant in City’s Treble campaign

Bruno Fernandes had equalised for United at Old Trafford in January 2023, despite Marcus Rashford seemingly interfering with play while stood offside

‘Sometimes it goes for you, sometimes it goes against you,’ Maresca said. ‘Three years ago when I was here, the same thing happened to us against Man United and we lost to them in the derby there.

‘The goal was not a regular goal if you remember. And no one apologises. We are still waiting for the apology for that. Sometimes it goes for and against.’

Maresca chose to shift focus on to City’s performance on Sunday, a result celebrated wildly in front of the away section, opening up an eight-point gap between the rivals after four games.

‘To talk about one moment after that game when we played for 70, 75 minutes with 10 players is quite poor,’ the Italian added. ‘I think the performance was unbelievable and I'm pleased.

‘It is not easy for the VAR and those in front of the screen who make a decision in 10-20 seconds. It is not easy for them. People make mistakes, I make mistakes, players make mistakes.

‘It is not easy to be in front of the screen and make a decision in 20 seconds, two minutes. It is complicated also for them.’

Sports.title: Man United academy star aims cryptic swipe at JJ Gabriel after teenager's quit threat - as teenager wipes ALL mention of Red Devils from his Instagram account
Sports.content:
Man United academy star aims cryptic swipe at JJ Gabriel after teenager's quit threat - as teenager wipes ALL mention of Red Devils from his Instagram account

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United fans have been left stunned after youngster Shea Lacey seemingly aimed a cryptic swipe at wantaway starlet JJ Gabriel.

United were rocked on Tuesday when it emerged that 15-year-old Gabriel, the jewel of their academy, wanted to leave.

The incipient talent, dubbed 'kid Messi', left the hierarchy shocked with his request and it is understood that he has been dropped for today's Carabao Cup match against Brighton.

And last night, Lacey appeared to stick the boot in with a viral post which has whipped up strong emotions among the fanbase.

Lacey, 19, simply shared a picture of him arriving at Old Trafford and a love heart emoji in a post which has now been viewed 5.9 million times.

United supporters came out in mass support in the comments, telling him 'you are the future' and 'you chose to stay at United, that's real passion my boy'.

Shea Lacey posted this cryptic tweet after the news that JJ Gabriel wants to leave Man United

Gabriel, 15, is considered one of English football's best talents but now wants to leave

By contrast, Gabriel's social media conduct has not endeared him to supporters after he wiped all reference to the club from his Instagram account.

It should be stressed that Gabriel is not fully accountable for his decision and image – like any player, he will have a family and agency team behind him who are heavily influential.

Daily Mail Sport's Oliver Holt has pinned the blame for his would-be exit on the club, asking why English football's hottest youth property would entrust his future to an institution in decline with controversial owners.

Less than a week ago, Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his UEFA League debut against FK Sabah, becoming the youngest player in United history to do so.

Last summer, when Gabriel flirted with an exit, director of football Jason Wilcox intervened. Along with head of negotiations Matt Hargreaves, he convinced Gabriel of his route to becoming the youngest-ever first-team player.

This season, Gabriel has been playing six years up and is thriving with the under-21s.

United sources believe there is still the possibility that the situation can be rectified given that despite the player’s request, he cannot be de-registered from the squad and his current contract runs until the end of the season.

Eyebrows were raised when it appeared Gabriel had wiped his Instagram account of all its photos and took out all mentions of Manchester United.

Gabriel, nicknamed 'Kid Messi', scored a hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League last week

Sources close to the player were quick to play down talk of discontent but it has now transpired that an explosive episode has been brewing behind the scenes, with Barcelona having spent years pursuing him, given he can leave the UK at 16 due to holding an Irish passport, allowing him to play in Europe.

Only days ago after scoring the European hat-trick Gabriel’s boss at youth level Adam Lawrence, who leads the Under-19s and the Under-21s, spoke about coaching a player like Gabriel.

‘I think the first thing in my job is not to ruin him,’ Lawrence said.

‘So when you have a talented player like JJ and the other lads of course, you obviously don't want to stifle their freedom and their creativity. And I think essentially what you try and do is to set the team up to allow the talent to function and to play free at the right moments.

‘Of course, it can't always be free and off the cuff in terms of some of the off-the-ball responsibilities that he's working on and some of the pressing things that he's thinking about. But again, in terms of how he plays properly and how he connects with other team-mates at the top end of the pitch, he's just in a real good space.

‘If you look at that game today, I think he's playing properly. I think he's trying to do the right things.

‘It's enjoyable working with him and challenging as a coach because the best players challenge you. When you work with talented players you have to find a way to help them and allow them to flourish and keep improving. Of course, there are things that you can keep working on but he is of course in a real good place.’

Asked about the people advising him, Lawrence was insistent those around him have the player’s best interests at heart.

The move has left United shocked and is a significant blow given how highly rated Gabriel is

‘With JJ, he's surrounded by people that really believe in him,’ Lawrence added.

‘From the top of the club right the way through. Where he's been at the club for so long, he's got good relationships with the players, with the staff.

‘Over the course of time that helps as well. At the moment just in terms of his game, his games programme, his training programme, making sure that he's getting the right exposure across different levels.

‘We're obviously not perfect but it's definitely something we put a lot of thought into. So yeah, it's good to see him just enjoying his football and in a good place for sure.’

But those comments come as scant consolation to supporters now with Gabriel determined to seek pastures new, particularly when a first team debut had long been earmarked for this week.

Sports.title: Silverstone set to avoid clash with Wimbledon final next year - with Bahrain to host 2027 curtain-raiser as F1 makes changes to calendar
Sports.content:
Silverstone will host the 2027 British Grand Prix on July 4, the Sunday that coincides with the middle weekend of Wimbledon, in a highlight of next year’s Formula One calendar that was released today

The schedule also names Bahrain as the opening round of the season, which will contain 10 sprints, up from six this year.

Bahrain is pencilled in for March 14 with Saudi Arabia coming the following weekend before the travelling circus decamps to Australia as part of a 24-race programme.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Silverstone bosses have willingly agreed to the early July date and that the circuit’s chief executive Stuart Pringle is content the overlap with Wimbledon is not a concern.

This collision of two iconic British sporting events has been the case in several recent years.

Despite the crossover this July, a crowd of 564,000 attended the Northamptonshire track over the weekend. It was the biggest attendance ever recorded at a Formula One event, eclipsing Adelaide in 1995.

The British Grand Prix won't clash with the Wimbledon's men's final next year as the Silverstone-based race will be held during the middle weekend of the SW19 action

Jannik Sinner won the men's Wimbledon final this year - with that showpiece and the British GP having collided in recent years

It is understood that the firm intention among F1 executives is that the first round will actually be staged in Bahrain, if world affairs allow, rather than be moved to Malaysia as is happening this year (‘the Bahrain GP in Kuala Lumpur’ on October 4) as the American/Israelian-Iranian war splutters on.

Monaco will stay in its new June slot, back a week from its traditional May date, and will host a sprint for the first time.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr REFUSE to display t-shirts supporting Spain's sovereignty of Ceuta amid migrant crisis - with Real Madrid stars divided over message
Sports.content:
A storm is brewing in Madrid after Real's two biggest stars, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr, concealed the club's message of Ceuta solidarity on pre-game t-shirts.

Far from putting on a united front on the issue, the pair, joined by Ibrahima Konate, deliberately rolled up their shirts to show their opposition to the club and league's stance.

The t-shirts displayed a 'We are all Caballas' slogan in support of the Ceuta community following the migration crisis in the Spanish North African enclave.

Earlier this summer, a state of emergency was declared when Spain faced a serious border crisis, with 80,000 migrants, mostly young Moroccan men, arriving on July 30 and 31. At least 57 people died trying to make the journey and Morocco has disputed Spanish sovereignty of the territory since independence in 1956.

The Ceuta president has said 13,000 of those migrants remain and it is still a red-hot political issue, which Real Madrid and other clubs have now waded in on.

Prior to their 3-2 win over Elche on Tuesday night, the whole squad were given t-shirts for an initiative designed to show solidarity with the residents of Ceuta.

Vinicius Jr (left) and Kylian Mbappe (right) showed their opposition to the message of Ceuta solidarity displayed on Real Madrid's t-shirts

Ibrahima Konate, Vinicius Jr and Mbappe were the only three players to roll up their shirts

In an embarrassing turn for Real, that message was then undermined by Mbappe, Vinicius Jr and Konate in front of the watching world.

The trio wanted to clearly demonstrate their opposition to the sentiment, deliberately hiding the slogan, effectively saying 'we do not agree with this stance.'

None of the players have come out publicly to explain their view on Ceuta but the pictures and footage from Tuesday evening speak volumes.

The rest of Jose Mourinho's squad posed for customary photos and lined up as usual ahead of the LaLiga clash kitted out in their specially designed green and white t-shirts.

Footage showed Vinicius Jr with his shirt rolled up to cover the message, before Mbappe grimaced when putting his on.

He then saw what Vinicius Jr had done and repeated the move.

The initiative for clubs to promote a message of Ceuta solidarity was put forward by league organisers for this round of fixtures.

No other players in the nine other fixtures over the weekend chose to demonstrate their protest to the Ceuta solidarity message.

Pictured: People play football at a settlement in Benitez Beach, created after the mass crossing of migrants from Morocco, in Ceuta, Spain, September 13, 2026

The three Real stars who opted to defy the club have angered plenty of supporters.

One wrote: 'I hope they boo them until the day they leave Real Madrid, utter disgust.'

Another posted: 'I hope Florentino fines them with 3 months' suspension without a job or pay. That way, the nonsense would end quickly. They're way too full of themselves.'

While a third gave his damning verdict: 'Shame that @realmadrid allows this contempt toward our compatriots from Ceuta by these millionaires who live in luxurious gated communities with private security.'

A Moroccan player for Real Betis in Seville, Ez Abde, also wore the t-shirt before his side's game against Villarreal and received a barrage of abuse online from his countrymen.

The issue is a hugely sensitive one and Ceuta's crisis has been front and centre of the political agenda in Spain since July.

Mbappe has not publicly spoken about his views on the migrant crisis in Ceuta

Spain is preparing accommodation for up to 10,000 migrants in Ceuta and the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, has insisted the situation was not mishandled. 'What happened is that we couldn't cope with the influx,' he said this week.

He added that authorities had taken in the migrants before returning the majority to Morocco, adding that nine in ten had gone back.

Sánchez said accommodation for 6,000 people would be available by the end of the week, with capacity eventually rising to 10,000.

He said the government hoped to have the situation under control by the end of the year and appealed for patience from residents of Ceuta, which has a population of around 84,000.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
