World.title: Ex-NBA President Nwokoye conferred with Blue Silk rank
World.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA—A former President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Chief Ebele Nwokoye, has been conferred with the Blue Silk rank, an honour introduced as an alternative to the Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) title for non-litigation lawyers in Nigeria.

The introduction of the title had been the subject of a legal battle between the NBA and promoters of the rank, the Association of Legislative Drafting and Advocacy Practitioners (ALDRAP).

Both the NBA and the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, had opposed the introduction of the “Blue Silks,” describing the title as illegal.

Likewise, the Legal Practitioners’ Privileges Committee (LPPC) disowned the Blue Silk title, insisting that the rank of SAN remained the highest mark of professional distinction for legal practitioners in the country.

Maintaining that the “Blue Silk” rank has no statutory backing, the LPPC warned that its use could amount to a violation of the provisions of the Rules of Professional Conduct for Legal Practitioners 2023.

However, the award of the rank to a former President of the NBA appears to be a major twist in the controversy.

Nwokoye, who served as NBA President from 1985 to 1987, was conferred with the Blue Silk rank on Tuesday at an event in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State.

He was also conferred with the title of National Patron of the Body of Senior Counsel of Nigeria (BOSCON).

BOSCON is the body responsible for the assessment and conferment of candidates who apply for the Blue Silk rank.

Unlike the rank of SAN, whose major criterion is the submission of evidence of courtroom litigation by candidates, the criteria for the Blue Silk rank require candidates to submit not less than 35 verifiable non-litigation transactions, as well as hold a Bachelor of Laws (LLB) degree for not less than ten years.

Reacting to the development in a statement, the Executive Secretary of ALDRAP, Dr Tonye Clinton Jaja, noted that September 15, 2026, will be remembered in the history of the Nigerian legal profession as the date the Blue Silk rank of Senior Counsel of Nigeria (SCN) secured a double victory.

“The conferment of the Blue Silks-SCN upon the former President of the NBA, Chief Nwokoye, is a significant victory, considering that the immediate past leadership of the NBA launched an unsuccessful attack against the Blue Silks-SCN at its inception in 2025.

“Instead of filing a lawsuit in a court of law, the Mazi Afam Osigwe-led regime of the NBA unsuccessfully tried to use illegal methods to stop the maiden investiture ceremony, which was held at the Federal Secretariat Complex, Abuja, Federal Capital Territory (FCT), on 15th December 2025.

“Without any court order, the Mazi Afam Osigwe-led NBA regime mobilised police officers and other officials of the National Assembly (including the Clerk to the National Assembly, Mr Kamoru Ogunlana, Esq.) to deny entry into the hall at the Senate building of the National Assembly, where the investiture ceremony was originally scheduled to hold.

“All the aforementioned illegal methods and the resort to self-help, instead of recourse to a court of law, by the Mazi Afam Osigwe-led regime of the NBA are what the Supreme Court of Nigeria condemned in its landmark judgment in Governor of Lagos State v. Ojukwu (1986) 1 Nigerian Weekly Law Reports (NWLR) (Pt. 18) 621.

“It must be noted that all these illegal methods were deployed by the Mazi Afam Osigwe-led regime of the NBA even after they were officially informed that the promoters of the Blue Silks-SCN had filed a lawsuit against the Incorporated Trustees of the NBA at the Federal High Court, Abuja, seeking an order of injunction against the NBA’s interference with the Blue Silks-SCN.

“Ironically, the same Mazi Afam Osigwe-led regime of the NBA immediately raised the alarm and relied on the defence that the Incorporated Trustees of the NBA is an independent legal entity that cannot allow external interference from the Hon. Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice. This was the same defence raised by Mazi Afam Osigwe during the July 2026 election of the National Officers of the NBA,” he stated.

Continuing, Jaja noted that the period within which the NBA could appeal the Abuja Federal High Court judgment affirming the conferment of the Blue Silks has passed.

“The second part of the victory is that the time prescribed for the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) to file its appeal has elapsed, and the NBA has failed to file any appeal against the said judgment, which validates the Blue Silks-SCN.

“The judgment was delivered on 27th January 2026 by Hon. Justice Mohammed Umar Garba of the Federal High Court, Abuja, Suit Number FHC/ABJ/CS/1238/2025,” he added.

According to him, the judgment prohibited the NBA, and by extension the LPPC, from attempting to regulate the Blue Silk rank and any other matters not expressly mentioned in the Legal Practitioners Act, 1962.

“The NBA, who were parties in the said lawsuit, failed to appeal that judgment. Therefore, it remains the binding judgment,” Jaja said, noting that instead of appealing, the NBA is relying on another judgment by a different judge of the same Federal High Court, Abuja, which has itself been appealed.

He insisted that the Blue Silk title, introduced as an alternative to the rank of SAN, is a legally recognised route to legal excellence for non-litigation lawyers in the country.

World.title: Rivers, Kwara, Gombe, Cross River: APC states threatened by Wike’s Rainbow Coalition ahead of 2027
World.content:
Powerful blocs within the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, are increasingly concerned about the spread of the National Rainbow Coalition, backed by Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, across states controlled by the ruling party.

The coalition, which Wike insists is primarily aimed at securing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, has nevertheless thrown up alliances involving opposition parties and politicians opposed to APC candidates at state and National Assembly levels.

The development has raised particular concerns in Rivers, Kwara, Gombe and Cross River, where coalition-backed candidates and political realignments are challenging existing APC structures.

APC governors and their allies are worried that the arrangement could create confusion among voters and weaken the party’s candidates in elections taking place alongside the presidential poll.

Wike, however, has maintained that his political objective is to support Tinubu while working with politicians across party lines.

Speaking during a media chat in Port Harcourt, Wike specifically accused Imo State Governor and Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum, Senator Hope Uzodimma, and Kwara State Governor and Chairman of the Nigeria Governors Forum, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, of campaigning against him.

“Take, for example, Kwara; he has been the one championing this campaign against me. Yes, I have confronted him too. I don’t talk about what I cannot defend,” Wike said.

He accused AbdulRazaq of alleging that he was sponsoring candidates against the governor’s preferred choices in Kwara while arguing that he had provided a political platform for aggrieved APC members who could otherwise have joined groups opposed to Tinubu.

The concerns among APC leaders are particularly pronounced in states where politicians who have fallen out with the ruling party are now working with the Rainbow Coalition.

Rivers

Rivers presents one of the most complicated fronts for the APC, with the coalition drawing members from the PDP, APC, Labour Party and other political groups.

The coalition emerged in January 2026 during the political crisis involving Wike and Governor Siminalayi Fubara. Its political significance increased after Fubara joined the APC.

The coalition has since generated uncertainty over the governorship race, particularly after it backed former PDP Minority Leader in the House of Representatives, Kingsley Chinda, for governor.

Chinda, who had been a PDP lawmaker, appeared before the APC screening committee after his defection, although the circumstances surrounding his move remain the subject of litigation.

The choice of Chinda has also reportedly generated disquiet among some coalition members from the riverine areas, who argue that a candidate from the area should have been preferred.

The coalition subsequently picked Major Jack, the current Majority Leader of the Rivers State House of Assembly, as Chinda’s running mate.

The arrangement has created a situation in which Rivers voters could face different candidates representing parties that are simultaneously claiming membership of the same coalition.

Kwara

Kwara has emerged as another major battleground between the APC structure and politicians aligned with Wike’s coalition.

The conflict intensified after a group of aggrieved APC members joined forces with former Senate President Bukola Saraki and the Wike-backed PDP structure in the state.

Senator Saliu Mustapha, who contested the APC governorship primary and later faced a battle over his return to the Senate, subsequently resigned from the APC and joined the PDP.

He was given the PDP ticket for Kwara Central, setting up a contest with Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq.

Another APC chieftain, Kolo Jiya, also left the party and joined the PDP, while two members of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Olushola Odetundun and Saba Yisa Gideon, defected to the PDP.

The aggrieved APC members subsequently came together under the Otoge Progressives, T.O.P., and formally launched the Kwara chapter of the National Rainbow Coalition on August 26, 2026.

The coalition says its arrangement allows politicians to support Tinubu for president while retaining the freedom to support different parties in other elections.

Gombe

In Gombe, former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Pantami, has moved to the PDP with the backing of the Rainbow Coalition.

The development has created another unusual political alignment, with the coalition seeking to support Tinubu at the presidential level while simultaneously working against APC structures at the state level.

The situation illustrates the central dilemma confronting APC leaders: politicians can support the president while campaigning against candidates of the party on whose platform he is seeking re-election.

Cross River

Cross River is another state where the coalition is challenging APC structures.

The PDP has an active governorship candidate, Arthur Jarvis, while the party also has candidates contesting senatorial, House of Representatives and House of Assembly seats.

About 500 APC members recently defected to the PDP in the state, according to the report.

Why APC governors are worried

The central concern among APC figures is that the Rainbow Coalition’s multi-party structure could undermine President Tinubu’s re-election.

Beyond this, the governors argued that ahead of the 2027 elections, Wike’s arraignment could weaken the APC and that they won’t support or endorse candidates who are not members of the party in the 2027 elections.

Speaking with journalists at the end of APC Governors Forum meeting on Monday night in Abuja, Imo state governor and secretary of the Tinubu Campaign Council, Hope Uzodimma, said, “The APC Governors Forum unanimously resolved that its members will not participate in, support or endorse any alliance or political arrangement capable of undermining the re-election of Mr President, weakening the APC or adversely affecting any candidate of the party at all levels.

“In other words, the forum has no intention to support any candidate at any level that is not an APC candidate because our candidates who are contesting the election are being sponsored by our party.”

He added that the APC’s campaign activities at all levels would focus exclusively on the party’s candidates and align with Mr Tinubu’s agenda.

“The governors’ campaign commitment is exclusively to all APC candidates. All levels of the party campaign architecture will align with the expectations of Mr President and the strategic objectives of the party.”

Wike has remained defiant

Wike, however, maintained that the Rainbow Coalition was created to mobilise support for President Tinubu’s re-election and had nothing to do with the APC or its candidates in other elections.

In a statement by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, the FCT minister insisted his support for 2027 was specifically for Tinubu and did not amount to a commitment that the PDP would not field candidates in other elections.

“What I said and stand for is that I will mobilise support for the re-election of the President. I never promised anyone that PDP will not field candidates to contest governorship, National Assembly and States House of Assembly elections,” Wike said.

He also dismissed the suggestion that the Rainbow Coalition was an arrangement with the APC, describing it as a platform for members of different political parties supporting Tinubu’s re-election.

“Most importantly, Rainbow Coalition has nothing to do with the APC. Rather, it is our own way of mobilising support across political parties for Mr President, who has done well to deserve a second term,” he added.

Wike further challenged Uzodimma over APC’s performance in the 2023 elections in Imo and other South-East states, questioning how the party won legislative seats despite recording a much lower share of the presidential vote.

“Was it Rainbow Coalition that also made APC to win National Assembly elections in Ebonyi, Abia and Enugu states where the president did not have ten per cent of the votes?” he asked.

World.title: Olu Jacobs was a national icon — Omokri
World.content:
Reno Omokri

Nigeria’s Ambassador-designate to Mexico, Reno Omokri, has described the late veteran actor, Oludotun Baiyewu Jacobs, popularly known as Olu Jacobs, as a national icon whose pioneering career on the international stage inspired generations of Nigerian actors.

Omokri, in a statement following the announcement of Jacobs’ death at the age of 84, said the late actor played a significant role in laying the foundation for the contemporary African film industry.

He said Jacobs broke international barriers long before Nollywood became a global phenomenon and brought pride to Nigerians through his performances in British television productions and international films.

“Oludotun Baiyewu Jacobs, better known as Olu Jacobs, was a National Icon and a source of pride for Nigeria, whose pioneering role as an international thespian inspired many of our countrymen and women and drew many of today’s stars into television and movie acting,” Omokri said.

Recalling his childhood memories, the ambassador-designate said Nigerians watched Jacobs feature in British television shows and international movies, noting that the actor received professional training at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art (RADA) in London.

“As children, we watched in awe as one of us starred in multiple British sitcoms and several global blockbuster movies,” he said, citing Jacobs’ appearance in the British television series, The Professionals.

Omokri also described Jacobs as one of the foundational figures of Nigeria’s modern film industry, placing him alongside his mentor, the late Chief Hubert Ogunde.

“Along with his mentor, the late great Chief Hubert Ogunde, he was the real Grand Old Man of Nollywood, having become a global star as far back as the seventies and early eighties,” he said.

He cited Jacobs’ appearances in international productions including The Dogs of War, in which he starred alongside Hollywood actor Christopher Walken, and Roman Polanski’s Pirates.

Omokri further said Jacobs’ humility had contributed to some people making claims to the title of Nollywood pioneer, but maintained that the actor’s body of work spoke for itself.

“Because of the modesty of Ogunde and Jacobs, and especially Mr Jacobs, who starred in hundreds of Nollywood movies, less deserving individuals have made pretences to their title of Nollywood Pioneers, but history makes their claims hollow,” he said.

Mourning the veteran actor, Omokri offered his condolences to Jacobs’ family, particularly his wife, veteran actress Joke Silva, and their children.

“We pray that God Almighty grant the family he left behind succour, especially Auntie Joke Silva, his wife and fellow actor, and their children,” he said.

Omokri also expressed gratitude that Jacobs was honoured by the Nigerian government during his lifetime with the Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR) national honour.

World.title: Tshisekedi third-term proposal sparks protests in DRC
World.content:
Dozens of people have been arrested in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) following protests against a proposed constitutional amendment that could allow President Felix Tshisekedi to seek a third term.

The protests broke out on Tuesday in Kinshasa, the capital, and several other major cities, with police using force to disperse demonstrators.

According to Reuters, police fired tear gas and warning shots in Kinshasa to disperse hundreds of protesters who participated in the demonstrations.

Videos shared on social media showed protesters waving flags belonging to various political parties during demonstrations organised by Coalition Article 64 (C64), a broad opposition alliance opposed to the proposed constitutional amendments.

Tshisekedi, who has been president since 2019, is due to complete his second five-year term in 2028. Under the current constitution, he would be ineligible to seek another term.

However, the 63-year-old president said last month that he would be willing to serve a third term in the conflict-plagued country “if the people wish it.”

In June, months before Tshisekedi made the remarks, the DRC Senate passed a bill providing for the holding of referendums in the country.

The protests reportedly escalated after supporters and opponents of Tshisekedi clashed during demonstrations over the proposed constitutional changes, prompting police to intervene.

Martin Fayulu, a former presidential candidate and one of the leaders of C64, said the opposition was considering filing an international complaint against Tshisekedi over the alleged violence against opposition activists.

World.title: Kara Bridge repairs trigger Lagos-Ibadan gridlock
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Motorists and commuters have been stranded along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway following ongoing rehabilitation works on the Kara Bridge, located around the Lagos-Ogun border.

The development has resulted in heavy traffic congestion along the expressway, with motorists reportedly spending extended periods on the highway.

A viral video circulating on Wednesday showed motorists trapped in the gridlock, with one of them describing the situation as a standstill.

According to reports, the stretch of the expressway from the 7Up area to Berger was completely blocked as of the time of filing this report.

A motorist identified simply as Lekan Oluwole lamented the situation, attributing the gridlock to the ongoing reconstruction of the Kara Bridge.

“Due to ongoing reconstruction on Kara Bridge, everywhere is being blocked and standing still along the stretch and environs,” he said.

World.title: 2027: Court gives Atiku 7 days to serve suit challenging Tinubu’s eligibility on APC
World.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

The Federal High Court sitting in Abuja on Wednesday issued an order for President Bola Tinubu to be served, within seven days, with the suit seeking to stop him from contesting the 2027 presidential election over his alleged submission of forged certificates to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

The court, in a ruling delivered by Justice Inyang Ekwo, approved substituted service of the legal process on President Tinubu through his political party, the All Progressives Congress (APC).

Justice Ekwo made the order after hearing a motion moved by Atiku’s lawyer, Mr. Olanrewaju Omotayo-Ojo, who stood in for Mr. Silas Onu, said to be bereaved.

The suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, was brought before the court by a former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Atiku Abubakar.

While the ADC was joined as the 2nd plaintiff, President Tinubu, the APC, and INEC were listed as the 1st to 3rd defendants, respectively.

Specifically, Atiku, in a 25-paragraph affidavit he personally deposed to in support of the suit, alleged that President Tinubu submitted a bogus National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate to INEC in support of his qualification for the presidential seat.

Insisting that President Tinubu gave false information about himself in the Form CF0001 he submitted to INEC, the plaintiffs drew the court’s attention to the fact that the NYSC certificate he submitted to the electoral body bears the name “Tinubu Bola Adekunle.”

“I know that the NYSC certificate is clearly not one obtained by the 1st defendant, as it belongs to one Adekunle.

“The said NYSC certificate, bearing the name Tinubu Bola Adekunle, is herein attached and marked as Exhibit P2.

“I know that the said NYSC certificate is still in existence and in the custody of the 3rd defendant (INEC), and that it is a forgery, as the 1st defendant’s name is not Adekunle, and yet he submitted it to the 3rd defendant to be acted upon as genuine,” Atiku averred.

He told the court that Tinubu had been parading the forged certificate since 1999, when he contested the Lagos State governorship election.

Atiku therefore urged the court, among others, to determine: “Whether, in view of the limitations in section 138(1)(a) & (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, and section 285(14)(c) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (As Amended), the Plaintiffs will not be allowed to enforce the binding provision of section 137(1)(j) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (As Amended), which applies, mutatis mutandis, to all candidates aspiring to the office of President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.”

As well as: “Whether the 1st and 2nd Defendants should be disqualified for presenting a forged NYSC certificate to the 3rd Defendant for the 2023 and 2027 Presidential Elections, in breach of section 137(1)(j) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (As Amended).”

Upon a positive determination of the legal questions, the plaintiffs sought a “declaration that the 1st Defendant presented a forged certificate to the 3rd Defendant when he contested for Governor of Lagos State in 1999, and thereby breached the provision of section 137(1)(j) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (As Amended).”

Likewise: “An order disqualifying the 1st and 2nd Defendants from participating in the 2027 Presidential Election, for presenting a forged certificate to the 3rd Defendant when the 1st Defendant contested for Governor of Lagos State in 1999.”

The court had earlier slated September 28 to commence full-blown hearing of the case.

The INEC has since filed processes challenging the competence of the suit, which it urged the court to dismiss.

However, it appears two Senior Advocates of Nigeria (SANs) may be on a collision course over who was briefed to represent President Tinubu in the matter.

Even though the plaintiffs had insisted on effecting personal service of the suit on President Tinubu, a former Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Chief Akin Olujinmi, SAN, and a former President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN, have separately filed processes for the 1st defendant.

The two senior lawyers separately challenged the competence of the suit and Atiku’s locus standi (legal right) to query the credentials Tinubu submitted to INEC, citing provisions of Section 29(5) of the Electoral Act 2026.

In a counter-affidavit filed on Tinubu’s behalf, Chief Olujinmi, SAN, contended that Atiku’s case had become statute-barred, noting that the certificates were submitted to INEC before August 1 and the 14-day period allowed for such litigation had elapsed.

Besides, he argued that Atiku, being a member of the ADC, has no legal right to challenge what was done by the APC.

Likewise, Chief Olanipekun, SAN, who also identified himself as Tinubu’s lawyer, filed both a preliminary objection and a counter-affidavit seeking dismissal of the suit, which he maintained is incompetent and a gross abuse of court process.

In a letter dated September 10, addressed to the Deputy Chief Registrar of the court, Chief Olanipekun, SAN, said he had been briefed by President Tinubu to lead a team of counsel to represent and defend his interests in the matter.

The letter, a copy of which was sighted by Vanguard on Wednesday, read in part:

“On or about 14th August, 2026, the public was inundated with news reports of not just the filing of the action, but also narratives of the issues purportedly submitted for the court’s consideration by the plaintiffs.

“Despite this, our client has not been served with the originating processes till date. When our client got wind that the matter would be coming up for mention before the Honourable Court on 1st September, 2026, he instructed us to appear for him, pursuant to which a member of his legal team, Prince Omosanya Popoola, SAN, appeared in court, not only to represent him, but also to collect the processes filed by the plaintiffs on his behalf, as per his instruction.

“The appearance of Prince Omosanya Popoola, SAN, on the said day is on the court’s record. Surprisingly, the plaintiffs’ counsel objected to this harmless but very reasonable application by counsel to collect the processes in open court.

“To date, our client remains the only party that has not been served with the originating processes. Further to the foregoing, we hereby (on our client’s instruction) formally apply that the court provide us with either the service copy (of the originating processes) meant for our client or a certified true copy of the said originating processes, to enable the immediate filing of his response to the plaintiffs’ suit.

“This is not only in furtherance of his right to a fair hearing, but also in demonstration of the fact that our client has nothing to hide.

“Kindly bring this letter to the urgent attention of the Honourable Presiding Judge.

“We undertake to pay the necessary fees for the certified true copies,” the letter added.

The plaintiffs have also applied to be allowed to effect some amendments to the suit, especially to change the name of the INEC form that President Tinubu allegedly attached the forged certificates to, which was wrongly referred to as Form CF001 instead of Form EC9.

World.title: 2027: Nigeria traumatised, needs experienced ‘father figure’ like Atiku — ADC
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has described Nigeria as a traumatised country that needs experienced political leaders such as its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to steer the country through its current challenges.

Bolaji Abdullahi, the party’s National Publicity Secretary, made the submission on Tuesday during an interview with News Central, while defending the choice of Atiku and former Rivers State governor, Rotimi Amaechi, as the party’s presidential and vice-presidential candidates for the 2027 election.

Abdullahi was responding to questions about how the ADC ticket differed from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), particularly with both Atiku and Amaechi having previously held public offices.

He argued that holding political offices in the past should not automatically disqualify anyone from seeking office again, saying Atiku’s experience could be particularly useful given Nigeria’s current condition.

He likened Nigeria’s situation to that of South Africa after the end of apartheid, when the African National Congress (ANC) chose Nelson Mandela, despite the presence of younger politicians within the party.

“There were younger people within the African National Congress, but for a nation that had been traumatised, the party recognised that it needed someone of a father figure, someone with experience, with maturity,” Abdullahi said.

He said the ADC considered Atiku capable of playing a similar role in Nigeria because of his political experience and understanding of the country’s history.

“For a traumatised country like Nigeria, because Nigeria has been traumatised. We’ve lost more people to terrorism, to banditry than we’ve ever lost at any other time in our history as a country,” he said.

Abdullahi also cited worsening economic conditions, arguing that Nigerians were poorer than they had been previously.

He said Atiku’s experience, combined with Amaechi’s energy, would provide what he described as the balance required to address the country’s challenges.

“You need someone with the quality of experience that Alhaji Atiku Abubakar brings. You need someone with the energy and the drive of a Rotimi Amaechi to back it up,” he said.

World.title: Mayo and Da Silva out, Kaizer Chiefs relying on Godspower
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have two strikers out due to injury and at times, they were forced to play without strikers.

In recent weeks, coach Fernando Da Cruz has brought in Nigeria striker Etiosa Ighodaro.

The 25-year-old is yet to find the net this season, having returned fron an injury. In the few matches he’s played, the forward, who’s middle name is Godspower, has shown promise and is expected to start most games until Khanyisa Mayo and Flavio Silva return.



Against Polokwane City, Ighodaro has a decent game but failed to find the back of the net.

Former Kaizer Chiefs winger Junior Khanye felt the striker had an impact but lacked the skills to bring something different to the team.

“A striker can put in a solid performance without scoring goals. Ighodaro put in a performance that says he wants to start the next game.

“But as a striker, you must be able to make space for yourself. You must be skilful, take somebody on and take a shot.

“For me, if there was a better striker, they would release Ighodaro because there’s not much that he is adding at Kaizer Chiefs.”

Amakhosi‘s last match was a 1-1 draw against Polokwane City. The draw saw them drop to fourth in the Betway Premiership after six matches played.



Can Kaizer Chiefs still challenge for the league?

So far, the Glamour Boys are eight points behind Mamelodi Sundowns but have two games in hand. A further drop in points could see their league ambitions coming to an end early in the season.

World.title: Orlando Pirates vs Durban City: Starting XI and score predictions
World.content:
Pirates are back to the bread and butter of Betway Premiership action. Photo: Pirates Official Facebook

Defending Betway Premiership champions Orlando Pirates get back to domestic business this week. How will they line up against Durban City?

Pirates return to South African bread and butter

Orlando Pirates are back in Mzansi after vanquishing Mauritian side La Cure Waves FC. Next on the agenda for the Sea Robbers is a home clash with Durban City. Here’s how we think they’ll line up:

Pirates’ predicted XI vs Durban City: Chaine; Sebelebele, Seema, Zulu, Ndaba; Mthiyane, Dansin; Kgositsile, Selepe, Appollis; Mbuthuma.



Reminder of the Starting XI vs La Cure Waves: Chaine; Sebelebele, Seema, Zulu, Rapoo; Mthiyane, Mokobodi; Kgositsile, Masilela, Appollis; Mbuthuma.

Also read: Rele Mofokeng to leave Belgium for a superior European league

Orlando Pirates are sitting pretty in the league

The Buccaneers came from a goal down to win 3-1 against La Cure Waves FC thanks to strikes from Kabelo Kgositsile, Kamohelo Sebelebele and Yanela Mbuthuma. Pirates face Durban City in the league on Thursday, 17 September. Kickoff is at 19:30. 24-year-old Mbuthuma has scored three goals in his last three outings and should retain his place ahead of Boitumelo Radiopane. City are a stubborn opposition, drawing three of their five league matches so far, but we expect Pirates to wear them down and claim three more points.

Prediction: Pirates 2-0 Durban City

What’s the situation at the summit of the table?

Sundowns remain top with 20 points after eight matches. Pirates are second with 13 points, but have three games in hand on the Brazilians. AmaZulu’s impressive start sees them third on 13 points after six games, while Chiefs sit fourth with 12 points after six outings.

World.title: Orlando Pirates to face Namibian champions in a different country
World.content:
Orlando Pirates’ opponents African Stars will trravel away for their home game. They do not currently have a CAF approved stadium in Namibia that meets the required international standards.

The Namibian champions were forced to play their previous home fixture in Mzansi. It was against AS Mangasport at the Lucas Masterpieces Moripe Stadium in Pretoria.

AFRICAN STARS TAKE ORLANDO PIRATES TO BOTSWANA

Stars have confirmed the first leg is scheduled for 17 October at the Botswana National Stadium in Gaborone. The match is listed for 3pm Namibian time.



That means Orlando Pirates will travel to Botswana rather than Namibia for the first meeting. African Stars booked their place in the second preliminary round after completing a dramatic comeback against AS Mangasport.

The Namibian champions lost the first leg 3-1 in Gabon, leaving themselves with a difficult task in the return fixture.

They responded with a 2-0 victory to level the tie at 3-3 on aggregate. The result was progression on the away goals rule. Their stadium situation has now become a major factor in the next stage of their Champions League campaign.



Instead of welcoming Orlando Pirates in Windhoek, African Stars are expected to stage their home fixture outside Namibia once again. The latest information points towards the Botswana National Stadium in Gaborone.

African Stars will once again be unable to enjoy the traditional advantage of playing a continental home fixture in front of their supporters in Namibia.

Head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou spoke positively about remaining within the region for both matches, particularly during a busy period of the season.



It creates an unusual CAF Champions League tie for the Buccaneers. They will face the Namibian champions, but their away match will take place in Botswana rather than Namibia.

For African Stars, the lack of a CAF approved home stadium remains a significant challenge as they continue their continental campaign.

SECOND LEG COMING TO SOWETO

Orlando Pirates entered the second leg against Mauritian side La Cure Waves needing to finish the job after being held to a 0-0 draw in the first leg.



The Buccaneers then suffered an early scare at home when La Cure Waves took the lead in the sixth minute through Ivan Ami.

A 3-1 victory was enough to send the Sea Robbers through with a 3-1 aggregate victory and into the second preliminary round.

World.title: Formula One 2027 calendar revealed, includes Monaco sprint race
World.content:
The 2027 Formula One calendar unveiled on Wednesday will feature 24 Grands Prix across 22 countries and 10 sprint events, including Monaco. Image: Attila KISBENEDEK / AFP

The 2027 Formula One calendar unveiled on Wednesday will feature 24 Grands Prix across 22 countries and 10 sprint events, including Monaco.

Pre-season testing is scheduled to take place in Bahrain from February 24-27 before the first race is held there on March 12-14, followed by Saudi Arabia a week later.

READ | Lando Norris extends McLaren stay until 2030



Contingency plans

The FIA will be hoping that those events in the Gulf do not suffer the disruption they have experienced this year due to the repercussions of the US-led war on Iran.

This year’s season is scheduled to end with races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi but Formula One has contingency plans if those races cannot be held for safety reasons as a result of the ongoing conflict.

The 2027 season is also due to conclude in Abu Dhabi.



The European leg of the 2027 calendar includes the return of Portugal in June, with Turkey rejoining the calendar in October between the races in Azerbaijan and Singapore.

The Netherlands drops out of the calendar in 2027.

World.title: Lepas L6 1.5T Pantera review: Chery on TOP
World.content:
When we first climbed behind the wheel of a Lepas L6 1.5T Pantera, pricing was yet to be decided in South Africa. As such, that vehicle, with barely 100km on the odometer, had no accurate market positioning. Yes, it is a handsome, quiet and tidy crossover SUV. But does it cost R700k or R300k, you know?

When you’re dealing with a brand South Africans have not yet heard of, that context means a lot. However, a few months down the line, we finally know the number attached to the Lepas L6 1.5T Pantera DCT. It’s R499 900. And all of a sudden, the picture gets a whole lot clearer …

LEPAS L6 1.5T PANTERA DCT

A sporting countenance that isn’t exactly delivered upon with modest ICE outputs. Image: Ray Leathern

Lepas is the newest addition to what’s become a genuinely sprawling local operation for the Chery Group. Six separate badges in South Africa alone: Chery, Omoda, Jaecoo, Jetour, iCaur and now Lepas. Fascinatingly, each runs as its own branded entity, with its own PR and marketing departments. However, each shares common underpinnings with the same Wuhu-based parent company in China.



As odd as it sounds, this multi-badge strategy is paying off in a big way. Individually, Chery sits around sixth on Naamsa’s monthly sales charts. Give or take a few hundred sales fluctuation, it trades places with GWM as the top-selling Chinese marque in the country. But add up sales across all the group’s sub-brands, and the combined tally pushes the Chery Group into second place overall in South Africa’s passenger vehicle market.

WHAT R500K GETS YOU

This is where the real value can be felt, the comfortable and well-appointed cabin. Image: Ray Leathern

Plus, the group’s recent takeover of Nissan’s old Rosslyn plant in Pretoria only underlines how serious it is. This is group that’s growing roots in South Africa. Nevertheless, for the money, the Lepas L6 1.5T Pantera cuts no corners. Standard equipment includes 19-inch alloys on Kumho rubber, a panoramic sunroof, quilted leather seats all round. The cabin is dominated by a 13.5-inch touchscreen that, refreshingly, runs a clean, responsive interface rather than the laggy, menu-heavy systems that plague some similar offerings.

Ease of use and practicality is a genuine strength of the Lepas L6 1 5T Pantera. Boot space runs to 435 litres with the rear seats up, expanding to 1 255 litres folded flat. This is more than enough for a family SUV and the overall cabin space provides plenty of head and leg room for taller occupants. A week behind the wheel showed no build-quality issues whatsoever.

HOW DOES IT DRIVE?

Side bar … this might be the first orange car we’ve ever reviewed. Not opposed. Image: Ray Leathern

Under the bonnet sits a 1.5-litre turbo petrol producing 108 kW and 225 Nm, sent through a six-speed dual-clutch automatic. That’s not a lot of output for a turbo motor, and it’s not a quick car as a result. This is at odds with its sporty looking orange paintwork. It is pretty hesitant as the gearbox works through various speed ranges. And there is no way to override the gearbox manually either.

At least the steering is nicely weighted though, and the Kumho tyres grip keenly enough through corners. But the standout, genuinely, is its refinement. Cabin noise, vibration and harshness suppression is premium level, excellent for a car price below R500k. Claimed/combined consumption sits at 7.2 l/100 km, however, in the real world we recorded an average of 8.5 l/100 km. Truthfully, the engine felt like it still needed some loosening up, so this may come down over time.

THE VERDICT

Lone one-piece rear light bar is almost becoming generic on these vehicles. Still looks the business though. Image: Ray Leathern

At R499 900, the Lepas L6 1.5T Pantera reframes what a well-specced, quiet and spacious family SUV should be on South African roads. It is not particularly memorable to drive, and it doesn’t need to be. For buyers cross-shopping in this segment, the Chery Group is increasingly dominate from multiple angles. For the longest time, the Chinese copied legacy carmakers. One wonders how long it’ll be before the legacy brands start to copy the Chinese’s effective multi-brand approach?

World.title: ‘He kidnapped himself’ – Mokoena recalls Punch Masenamela’s R1 Million stunt
World.content:
Former Mamelodi Sundowns winger Lebohang ‘Cheeseboy’ Mokoena has recalled a bizarre incident involving his former teammate Punch Masenamela, who allegedly faked his own kidnapping in an attempt to get R1 million from the club.

Masenamela made his name at Kaizer Chiefs before joining Sundowns in 2011, where he spent three years. Mokoena was part of the Sundowns squad during the former left-back’s time at the club.

Speaking on Soccerbeat, Mokoena recalled how Masenamela allegedly claimed he had been kidnapped while the team was preparing for a weekend fixture.



“We were training in the week preparing for the weekend’s game and Friday, when we arrived at camp, calls came in and we were told Punch Masenamela had been kidnapped,” Mokoena said.

Punch Masenamela spent three years at Chloorkop

“So we were all worried and tried to call him, asking ourselves, ‘What’s happening? Where’s Punch?’ Then Punch called and told the president [Patrice Motsepe] that he had been kidnapped and that the kidnappers were demanding a ransom,” Cheeseboy recalled.

“Okay, sharp, the chairman asked how much they wanted. He was like, ‘They want R1 million so they can let me go.’ He thought he was dealing with guys from the side corner who would just send the money.”



According to Mokoena, Sundowns took the claim seriously and began trying to establish Masenamela’s whereabouts.

“So Sundowns then told him they’d sort that out. They made signals, traced his call and found out that Punch was at a lodge in the Vaal. He was busy with room service the whole time and making calls, asking for ransom,” Mokoena said while laughing.

“They found him and he was alone and asked, ‘So you’re not kidnapped? Who kidnapped you? Ransom?’”



Mokoena revealed that Masenamela was later met with plenty of questions from his teammates when he returned to training.

“When he arrived at training, all the players wanted to know the story,” he added.

The former Sundowns players then decided to have some fun with the situation, presenting Masenamela with a briefcase and joking that it contained the R1 million ransom.



Mokoena said the senior players also made it clear to Punch Masenamela that he should never attempt anything similar again.

World.title: This Cape Town neighbourhood has been named one of the world’s coolest
World.content:
Kalk Bay has once again caught international attention, this time appearing among the world’s coolest neighbourhoods. Image: canva

Cape Town has once again found itself on the global travel map, with one of its best-known seaside neighbourhoods earning a place among the world’s coolest neighbourhoods for 2026.

Kalk Bay has been included in Time Out’s 40 coolest neighbourhoods in the world for 2026, putting the colourful coastal strip alongside neighbourhoods from cities around the globe.

The recognition highlights what locals and regular visitors have long loved about Kalk Bay: its mix of ocean views, old-world charm, independent businesses, art, food and a distinctly bohemian atmosphere.



A seaside neighbourhood that has kept its character

Located between the mountains and the ocean, the neighbourhood has a setting that is difficult to replicate.

The area is known for its harbour, where fishing remains part of everyday life, while the surrounding streets are packed with cafés, restaurants, shops and galleries.

Its coastal location also makes Kalk Bay popular with people looking to spend time outdoors. The mountains provide hiking opportunities, while the ocean draws surfers, swimmers and those simply wanting to enjoy the views.



Part of Kalk Bay’s appeal is that it has retained a strong sense of identity despite becoming a popular destination for visitors.

Its historic harbour remains one of the defining features of the area, while the surrounding buildings and narrow streets give it a distinctly different feel from Cape Town’s more modern neighbourhoods.

The area has also developed a reputation for its independent shopping and food scene, with everything from seafood and casual cafés to boutiques and art spaces.



That combination means visitors can spend a morning exploring the shops and harbour before heading into the mountains or settling down somewhere overlooking the water.

Kalk Bay’s place on the global list

Time Out‘s annual neighbourhood guide looks beyond the traditional tourist attractions of major cities, highlighting areas that offer a strong sense of local culture and character.

The top spot was taken by Jongno 3-ga in Seoul, South Korea.



For Cape Town, Kalk Bay’s inclusion puts the spotlight on a part of the city that many locals already know well.

It also adds another international accolade to a city that regularly attracts attention for its natural scenery, food and neighbourhoods.

For anyone exploring the Cape Peninsula, Kalk Bay offers a particularly easy combination of mountains, ocean, history, food and independent shops, all within a relatively small area.



And while its appearance on an international list may bring more attention to the neighbourhood, its appeal has little to do with the accolade itself.

Kalk Bay has been doing its own thing for years.

World.title: Here’s who will referee Springboks vs Wallabies Test in Perth
World.content:
The Springboks will have little time to celebrate their historic series victory over the All Blacks, with their next Test around 10 days away. Image: Italian Rugby Federation

The Springboks will have little time to celebrate their historic series victory over the All Blacks, with their next Test around 10 days away.

South Africa will face Australia in a one-off Test at the Optus Stadium in Perth on Sunday, 27 September, with kick-off scheduled for 11:30 (SA time).

Chance for fringe players?

The match is expected to provide an opportunity for several fringe players, with head coach Rassie Erasmus likely to select a largely second-string squad after the demanding four-Test series against New Zealand.

The Perth clash will be followed by the Springboks’ end-of-year tour and the conclusion of the Nations Championship.

AGREE? | John Smit: Malcolm Marx is South Africa’s best ever hooker

World Rugby has confirmed the match officials for the one-off Test.

Italy’s Andrea Piardi will be the referee and he will be assisted by two New Zealanders, Ben O’Keeffe and James Doleman.

Matteo Liperini (Italy) will be in the TMO booth, while New Zealand’s Richard Kelly will be on Foul Play Review Officer duty.



Piardi has refereed the Springboks on one previous occasion, when they narrowly beat Argentina 29-27 at Twickenham in London in October 2025.

World.title: In hydropowered Bhutan, solar starts to rise
World.content:
THIMPHU - Engineer Rinzin Galley stands on a platform overlooking a former military shooting range on the edge of Bhutan's capital Thimphu, now home to a gleaming field of solar panels.

With abundant waterways, Bhutan has long relied on hydroelectric power to meet its electricity needs and stay carbon negative -- absorbing more planet-warming gases than it emits.

But demand is growing, and in winter, when rivers run low before the mountain melt arrives, Bhutan already relies on imported Indian electricity.

Climate change is also threatening the future of the glaciers that feed those rivers, adding impetus to a push for energy diversification.

"Solar projects are booming," said Rinzin, senior engineer at Norion Renewable Energy.

The company's biggest project to date is the Dechencholing solar farm on former military land, with an installed capacity of 4.45 megawatts (MW).

Dechencholing is one of several solar fields developed in recent years, including the country's first mega project -- Sephu, with over 22 MW capacity.

That is relatively modest, especially compared to the vast solar fields installed in neighbouring China.

But it represents a new direction for Bhutan, where hydropower exports account for up to 15 percent of GDP, according to the World Bank.

World.title: Helen Mirren delves into Patricia Highsmith's mind in 'A Talent for Murder'
World.content:
TORONTO - Helen Mirren makes no secret of her admiration for writers, something reflected in her portrayal of American author Patricia Highsmith in "A Talent for Murder," the thriller that premiered at the Toronto Film Festival.

"It was a fascinating journey to go into her psychology," the 81-year-old British Oscar winner commented this week at a roundtable with journalists.

In "A Talent for Murder," Mirren embodies Highsmith, the author of the Tom Ripley novels, who moved in the 1980s to a small town in Switzerland, where she led an increasingly secluded life.

Directed by Anton Corbijn, the film presents a psychological duel between the renowned writer and her agent, Edward Ridgeway (Alden Ehrenreich), who tries to convince her to write a new Tom Ripley novel.

"Playing Highsmith was intense," Mirren told AFP.

Although there wasn't much audiovisual material available, the actor found clues to portray the reclusive writer in interviews and videos.

In that process, Mirren discovered she had nothing in common with her character.

"I've gone in the opposite direction in my attitude to life. She became very embittered, very private, isolated," Mirren said of Highsmith. "She was not a very nice person at the end of her life at all."

Likewise, the idea that anyone is capable of committing a crime is inconceivable to Mirren.

"I've never thought of killing a person. I don't think Patricia Highsmith is right about that," she said.

And the film doesn't hide that side of her personality.

"One wants to pay respect to her genius and her brilliance," Mirren said. "But I think it would do her a disservice to try and smooth over the edges that she very much had."

World.title: China warns against space 'battlefield' after US says weapons deployed
World.content:
BEIJING - China warned against turning outer space into a "battlefield" and Russia said it must be "free from any weapon" after the United States confirmed for the first time that it has arms deployed in orbit above the Earth.

Analysts said that the revelation by Washington confirmed an open secret but the timing of the announcement risked exacerbating tensions with Beijing and the risk of a weapons race in space.

The announcement marked a new stage in the major powers' rush for military space capabilities, driven by rapid technological advancements but lacking a comprehensive legal framework.

"The US has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action," a US Space Force spokesperson said in a statement that did not provide specifics on the weapons.

China's foreign ministry opposed the move, warning against the "weaponisation of outer space, turning it into a battlefield, as well as an arms race there".

"We urge the US side to stop expanding its military capabilities and preparing for war in outer space," ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a news briefing.

Russia called Tuesday for space to be kept "free of any weapons".

"We are counting on broad international consolidation to continue working toward the complete demilitarisation of space," said Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov.

- What are the US capabilities? -

The US statement did not provide concrete details about what weapons are deployed in space and how many.

"Space control encapsulates the mission areas required to contest and control the space domain -- employing kinetic and non-kinetic means to affect adversary capabilities," the statement said.

"These capabilities can be employed for offensive and defensive purposes," it added.

Non-kinetic means could include lasers to blind satellites, or even electromagnetic or cyber jamming of their data links.

- Why does the US want weapons in space? -

For Washington, both Russia and China -- its two main geopolitical rivals -- pose potential threats to US interests in space.

China "develops and operates space and counterspace capabilities as part of a military modernisation strategy," according to the US Space Force.

Russia, meanwhile, "views space as a warfighting domain and believes space supremacy will be a decisive factor in future conflicts", it said.

The militarisation of space is as old as the space race itself -- as soon as the USSR's Sputnik was launched into orbit as the first probe in space in 1957, Washington and Moscow began exploring ways to both arm and destroy satellites.

India in March 2019 said it had destroyed a low-orbiting satellite, following in the footsteps of Russia, China and the US, in a missile test that proved the nation was among the world's most advanced space powers.

- How might China react? -

Song Zhongping, an independent military commentator based in Hong Kong and former Chinese army instructor, told AFP the announcement was "no surprise at all" as the fact that the US possesses such weapons "has long been an open secret".

"The only difference is that the US used to keep it ambiguous, whereas now it has gone public, which shows that Washington is no longer trying to hide it," he added.

"China will not stand by and do nothing", he warned, noting Beijing already has its own space station in orbit.

"Whether China deploys weapons in space will depend entirely on whether the United States moves in that direction," he said.

The Wall Street Journal said Beijing supplied Iran with satellite imagery that enabled Tehran to precisely target military facilities and kill US service members in Jordan in July -- a claim China has denied.

- Can weapons in outer space be regulated? -

The biggest worry was once about nuclear weapons in space, but the superpowers and other countries signed the Outer Space Treaty in 1967, banning weapons of mass destruction in orbit.

Since then, Russia, the United States, China and India have explored ways to fight in space outside of that treaty, including by targeting rivals' satellites, which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation.

"There is a regulatory vacuum because Article 4 of the 1967 treaty only forbids weapons of mass destruction and nuclear weapons in orbit," said space law expert Laetitia Cesari.

She said the topic would likely be on the agenda at the next UN disarmament meeting in November.

"Moscow and Beijing have been wanting to work for about twenty years on a treaty to prevent the placement of weapons in space," while "Western states are trying instead to work on the notion of responsible behaviour," Cesari said.

The US announcement "will likely give impetus to the restrictive approach that Moscow and Beijing are pushing for," she added.

World.title: ANC fails in bid to get 181 candidates onto election ballot
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Electoral Court has dismissed the ANC’s appeal to have 181 councillor candidates included on the ballot after the party missed the candidate submission deadline.

The ruling means the affected candidates will not contest the local government elections on 4 November.

The dispute centred on the ANC’s candidate list submissions for six municipalities. The party challenged the IEC’s decision to exclude its candidates, arguing that it had not missed the deadline.

READ | ANC branches protest disputed ward councillor candidate lists

The ANC said technical glitches in the IEC’s electronic system prevented it from finalising its submissions on time. The IEC rejected the explanation.

The commission is expected to publish the final list of candidates on Wednesday.

Elections analyst Wayne Sussman said the ruling was a setback for the ANC ahead of the elections.

“This means that in key ANC strongholds like Port St Johns and Ngquza Hill Local Municipality, they will not have any ward or proportional representation councillors. That is a setback for ANC activists, councillors and the people who planned to vote for the party on election day,” Sussman said.

“This is not a good day for the ANC; they’ll need to bounce back and focus on getting everything right so they can have the best possible result on 4 November.”

The ANC said it will appeal the Electoral Court ruling.

World.title: Ekurhuleni killings: Second victim formally identified
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Another victim in the Ekurhuleni killings has been formally identified.

Itumeleng Kekana was reported missing on 17 July and is the second of the eight women whose bodies have been discovered across the East Rand to be formally identified.

Originally from QwaQwa in the Free State, Kekana’s identification brings some answers to a family that has been desperately searching for her.

But it also raises further questions about the circumstances surrounding her death and whether there could be a link between the cases.

Police have not confirmed that the deaths are connected, as investigations continue.

Seasoned investigators have been brought in to assist with the probe following the discovery of the women’s bodies across Ekurhuleni over the past two months.

World.title: Ekurhuleni murders: Activist says women need more than statements and campaigns
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - With all its policies and laws, South Africa has regressed when it comes to the treatment of women.

This is according to activist and advocate Brenda Madumise-Pajibo.

Women are killed every day in South Africa, with many of these cases never making headlines.

Therefore, Madumise-Pajibo says, the discovery of the bodies of eight women in Ekurhuleni does not come as a shock.

“It is just that it has come out in the open in the manner that it has,” she says.

“There are thousands of women who have suffered at the hands of their partners by being brutally assaulted and eventually killed,” she says.

The discovery of the women’s bodies in the East Rand followed calls for searches for missing runner Elizabeth ‘Tsontso’ Moselakgomo.

A woman wearing running clothes was found in a grassy area in Rhodesfield, Kempton Park, on Saturday.

World.title: 'Broader attack': Analyst warns of escalating US pressure on South Africa
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Pressure is mounting between Washington and Pretoria.

The Trump administration has introduced new visa restrictions targeting South African officials, adding another layer of tension to an already strained relationship.

Washington says the measures are linked to allegations of discrimination against white South Africans, as well as concerns surrounding South Africa’s Expropriation Act.

Pretoria has rejected those allegations.

But international relations analyst Kingsley Makhubela believes the dispute could extend far beyond visa restrictions.

Makhubela says the latest move could form part of a broader challenge to the South African government’s international standing.

“The Trump administration is setting up South Africa for a much broader attack on the legitimacy of the South African government,” Makhubela says.

He says one possible consequence could be increased pressure on South Africa’s participation in the African Growth and Opportunity Act, or AGOA.

According to Makhubela, Washington could use what it regards as South Africa’s failure to meet conditions set by President Donald Trump as justification for further restricting its participation.

But he says there is a bigger geopolitical picture at play.

South Africa’s strategic position at the southern tip of Africa, particularly its proximity to the Cape of Good Hope shipping route, could become increasingly significant amid developments in the Middle East and disruptions to global trade routes.

For Makhubela, this means Pretoria faces a delicate geopolitical balancing act.

He argues that South Africa should avoid viewing its international relationships as a choice between the United States and emerging global powers.

Instead, he says, Pretoria needs to navigate an increasingly multipolar world without becoming overly dependent on pressure from any one side.

World.title: Muthaiga Golf Club restores access after KFS standoff
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Muthaiga Golf Club has restored access to a section of its course that was temporarily taken over by the Kenya Forest Service (KFS), hours after the agency moved into the area, claiming it forms part of Karura Forest.

The disruption affected the Front Nine, covering Holes Two to Nine, before the club’s board intervened to restore normal operations.

In a statement issued Tuesday, Muthaiga Golf Club Chairman Dennis Mwirigi said the board had taken the necessary steps to facilitate the resumption of activities after the temporary disruption.

“We are pleased to confirm that access to the affected part of the course has been restored and members may proceed with their scheduled activities as usual,” Mwirigi said.

He said the board remained committed to protecting the club’s interests, assets and members while addressing the matter through the appropriate channels.

The development follows an earlier communication to members informing them that KFS had taken over access to the affected section, claiming it was part of Karura Forest.

The club had initially said the Front Nine would not be accessible until further notice as it sought to resolve the matter. The driving range and parking areas were not affected.

The incident sparked criticism over the manner in which KFS handled the dispute, with Prof Karanja, Chairperson of Friends of Karura Forest, urging the agency to pursue dialogue and legal channels.

Prof Karanja said KFS should have first engaged the club’s management and clearly explained its claim over the disputed land instead of deploying dogs, guns and heavy security.

“If they don't agree that it was your land, go to court. The court will determine,” he said.

He questioned whether KFS had adequately demonstrated that the disputed section was forest land or explained how it was allegedly acquired by Muthaiga Golf Club.

“They should have come publicly and said, look, Muthaiga, that area and that area belong to the forest,” Prof Karanja said.

He said KFS should identify the specific portion of land it claims belongs to the forest and explain the basis of its claim before taking further action.

Prof Karanja argued that the dispute should be resolved through established legal procedures rather than force. “Trees are not protected by guns,” he said.

He described the deployment of armed personnel as the wrong way of resolving a land dispute and called for engagement between KFS and the golf club.

Prof Karanja also warned that actions by government agencies could have wider implications for the administration of President William Ruto, saying confrontational conduct could lead members of the public to associate such actions directly with the government.

“When government departments behave like this, everybody now starts thinking, oh, it's Ruto's whatever,” he said.

He further recalled a previous dispute involving Friends of Karura Forest, where he said armed personnel were deployed and the group removed from an area before senior government officials intervened.

According to Prof Karanja, officials from the Treasury and forestry departments eventually intervened and encouraged dialogue to resolve the matter.

He urged KFS to adopt a similar approach in the Muthaiga dispute, saying the agency and the club should present their respective claims and seek a court determination if they cannot agree.

For now, the restoration of access means members can resume their scheduled activities, while the underlying dispute over the contested section remains subject to further engagement between KFS and the club.
