World.title: Croatia to Get Most Modern Thermal Spa in Historic €42 Million project
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – Croatia is set to get its most modern and largest thermal spa as a historic 42 million euro project finally nears completion.

Works on Wellovar in Veliki Korenovo, the largest construction project in the history of Bjelovar worth €42 million, have entered the final stage. Poslovni reports that the enormous complex with a total of ten pools is already taking on its final appearance, and finishing works and system checks are currently underway before opening. Bjelovar Mayor Dario Hrebak regularly visits the construction site and emphasises that the focus is now on the details and on balancing and calibrating one of the most complex and modern heating, cooling and hot water systems in Croatia.

“Works on the largest thermal spa in Croatia, our Wellovar, are nearing completion. Only minor details remain, but this is one of the most complex and modern heating, cooling and hot water systems in Croatia. We now have to ensure that the entire system is balanced and calibrated. It is hard to say when we will open the doors. Our great wish is that it will be on the 29th of September, on the Bjelovar City Day, but it is very difficult to predict,” said Hrebak. He added that at this moment the exact opening date is not crucial; the most important thing is that the project is completed to a high standard.

“What matters is that everything we see is heading towards its final stage and that the people of Bjelovar will get a standard that 95 percent of other cities in Croatia do not have. Croatia will also get an excellent centre for the development of water sports,” he stressed. In addition to tourist and recreational facilities, Wellovar is also expected to play an important role in the development of sport. According to Hrebak, the facility has been designed to meet the standards for hosting national and international swimming and water polo competitions. “We are truly looking forward to it soon opening its doors and delighting our citizens, as well as all tourists and visitors with its facilities,” Hrebak concluded.

With the completion of this massive €42 million project, Bjelovar is set to gain a major new sports, recreational and tourist complex. Although the official opening date has not yet been confirmed, the city administration’s wish is for Wellovar to welcome its first visitors as early as the 19th of September, on Bjelovar’s City Day.

World.title: Croatia to Make Changes to ENC Usage as of March 1st, 2027
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – Croatia will make significant changes to ENC usage as of March the 1st, 2027, and drivers with multiple vehicles need to pay particular attention to what is coming.

The much anticipated new Croatian road toll collection system will use ENC technology, but also automatic licence plate recognition via cameras. Poslovni reports that for years now, ENC has been one of the simplest ways to pay motorway tolls across Croatia. You put the device in your car, drive through the marked lane, and the system automatically handles the payment. However, with the introduction of the new electronic toll collection system, one thing becomes much more important than before: the ENC will also be linked to the vehicle’s registration plate.

From the 1st of March 2027, when the new system starts operating, the vehicle’s registration number, data on the ENC device, and a valid means of payment will have to be registered in the system for the ENC model to be used. The law expressly stipulates that a driver using ENC must pass through the toll point in a vehicle whose registration plates are identical to those linked in the system to the ENC device in the vehicle. This means it will no longer be enough simply to take a working ENC device and put it in any car. Before driving, it will be important that the vehicle being used on the motorway is properly registered in the new system.

this is particularly important if you use one enc for multiple cars

The change is especially significant for those who currently use the same ENC in several cars. Under the current rules of Croatian Motorways, an ENC device for vehicle categories IA, I and II is not tied to a single registration number. It can be used in multiple vehicles of the same category, provided the same device is not used simultaneously in more than one vehicle. The new system introduces a different principle: the registration number becomes an integral part of the data linked to the ENC device. Therefore, drivers who currently simply move the ENC from one car to another will have to make sure that the registration of the vehicle they are using is correctly linked to the device in the Electronic Toll Collection System.

The law itself does not currently stipulate that one ENC can necessarily be linked to only one registration number. The detailed rules on use and changes to data will be regulated by the rules of the new system. However, it is clear that the previous practice of simply transferring the device without checking the registration will no longer be sufficient. The good news for existing users is that current ENC devices will not become unusable. The law obliges motorway operators to include ENC devices purchased before the establishment of the new system into the new ESNC no later than its start.

the new cameras will read license plates

The new toll collection system will use ENC technology as well as automatic licence plate recognition via cameras. For passenger cars and other light vehicles, drivers will be able to choose between the ENC model and a model based solely on the registration number and a registered means of payment. When using ENC, the system will therefore have data on both the device and the vehicle’s registration number. Cameras will record the vehicle’s passage and read the licence plates in order to identify the vehicle and verify payment. For drivers, this brings a new habit: before driving, it will no longer be enough simply to check whether the ENC is in the car and whether there are sufficient funds on the account. They will also have to make sure that the vehicle’s registration number is correctly registered in the system. This is precisely what could be particularly important for those who currently use one ENC in multiple cars.

World.title: adidas and HNS Unveil New Croatia National Team Kits
World.content:
adidas has unveiled the long-awaited new official kits for the Croatia national football team, the first set produced under a long-term partnership with the Croatian Football Federation (HNS).

Combining cutting-edge performance innovation with elements founded in Croatian culture and identity, the new kits celebrate the heritage, pride and passion that define Croatian football.

The unveiling marks the start of a new chapter for one of international football’s most recognizable national teams. Having cemented its place among the world’s leading footballing nations, Croatia will step out in an adidas kit for the first time as part of the partnership announced earlier this year.

HNS / adidas

The new home shirt offers a modern take on Croatia’s iconic red-and-white checkerboard pattern, one of the most striking visual symbols in international football. For the first time, letters from the Glagolitic alphabet — the oldest known Slavic script and an important symbol of Croatian cultural heritage — have been woven into the checkerboard design, running throughout the pattern to give one of Croatian football’s most recognizable emblems a fresh, contemporary twist. The back of the collar also features the word “HRVATSKA” written in Glagolitic script, further tying the shirt to Croatia’s cultural history.

The away shirt, meanwhile, draws inspiration from Croatia’s long tradition of lace-making, a craft passed down through generations and another significant part of the country’s cultural heritage. An intricate lace-inspired motif runs across the shirt’s navy base, offering a modern interpretation of that tradition. The design is completed by a collar detail bearing the word “HRVATSKA” in typography inspired by cross-stitch embroidery, linking the traditional craft to contemporary football design.

HNS / adidas

“These shirts are much more than innovative football kits and striking design. Working with adidas, we chose a design that perfectly combines local pride with a global perspective. Those are exactly the values Croatia has always stood for, and now a new generation of fans and players will carry them forward,” said Marijan Kustić, president of the Croatian Football Federation.

Both shirts were developed to meet the demands of football at the highest level and feature the latest adidas CLIMACOOL+ technology. Specially developed stretch fabrics and 3D body-mapping technology improve ventilation and breathability, helping players stay dry through high-intensity matches and in hot conditions. Perforated three-stripe panels and strategically placed mesh zones further boost airflow and comfort.

Croatia’s men’s national team will wear the new kits for the first time during the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures.

Alongside the new shirts, adidas is also launching a wider Croatia national team collection that includes shorts, socks, training wear and leisurewear, designed for fans who want to show their connection to the national team both on and off the pitch.

A video unveiling the new kits has been posted on the Instagram profiles of @adidasfootball and the Croatian Football Federation.

The new Croatia national team kits, along with the full HNS x adidas collection, are available to buy from today at the official HNS online store. Pick out your kit, step into a new era of Croatian football, and wear it with pride.

World.title: CRANE Forum 2026: Productivity as a European Priority, Judiciary as the Greatest Obstacle to Investment
World.content:
September the 15th, 2026 – The CRANE Forum 2026 was recently held, which welcomed around 200 guests from the fields of investment to politics, and from economics to financial institution representatives.

As stated, around 200 guests involved with the Croatian economy, entrepreneurs and investors, members of the Government, ambassadors and representatives of international financial institutions, as well as county prefects and mayors, gathered at the Tihočaj estate in the Žumberak – Samobor Hills Nature Park to discuss investment prospects and the frameworks in which they will be implemented.

In Jastrebarsko on the 12th of September 2026, the fourth CRANE Forum, organised by CRANE, the Croatian Association of Investors and Business Angels, was held. The location was the Tihočaj estate in the Žumberak – Samobor Hills Nature Park. Once again this year, the Forum brought together all levels of decision-making on a single investment in one place: 200 guests from the top of the Croatian economy, entrepreneurs and investors, members of the Government, ambassadors and representatives of international financial institutions, as well as county prefects and mayors.

“Since 2008, CRANE has been connecting entrepreneurs and investors and bringing together capital, knowledge and experience with those who make the decisions. For development and new investments, finding an investor is not enough. What is also needed is a state that cooperates and understands the vision, and a local environment that knows how to create the conditions for its implementation. That is why we do not build the Forum as a conference, but as a working meeting at which everyone who decides on a single investment is present,” said Davorin Štetner, President of CRANE.

The key topics of this year’s Forum were the new multiannual financial framework of the European Union after 2027, the tax system as a competitive advantage, the role of local self-government in attracting strategic investments, and investments in healthcare.

Speaking about what Croatia can expect from the EU’s multiannual financial framework after 2027, Nataša Mikuš Žigman, Minister of Regional Development and EU Funds, stressed that the priorities coming from Brussels are focused on security, defence and climate efficiency, but equally on investments in productivity and competitiveness. Croatia, she announced, has already begun preparing a future competitiveness investment programme that will combine public and private funds, with the aim of raising the productivity of the economy. Among the novelties are milder requirements for technical documentation at the application and contracting stage, the possibility for applicants with smaller tax debts not to be excluded from the procedure but to settle them before the decision on the award of support is made, and raising the threshold for the implementation of procurement procedures with simple procurement via the eKohezija platform. In the negotiations on the new multiannual financial framework, Croatia insists that administrative burden relief actually reaches end-users and does not remain only on the Brussels–Member State axis.

On the panel dedicated to the tax system, in which Tomislav Ćorić, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, Davor Baković, President of the Croatian Exporters Association and Chairman of the Management Board of Končar MT d.d., Davor Tremac, Executive Director of Fono, and Domagoj Kamenski, Executive Director of Kamgrad, participated, it was emphasised that the Croatian tax framework in itself is not an obstacle to growth, but in certain segments even represents a competitive advantage, with a corporate income tax rate lower than the average of developed countries and excellent incentives for investment and research and development.

That the tax rate is not decisive is also shown by comparison with the surrounding region: ahead of Croatia on investment attractiveness rankings are the Czech Republic and Slovenia, which have significantly higher corporate income tax rates. The key problem, as Tremac stressed, is distrust in the judiciary, because what is contracted on paper is difficult and slow to enforce before Croatian courts, and this has been pointed out for thirty years without progress. The price of this distrust is measured in capital that does not arrive: when the enforceability of contractual protections is not certain, investors do not abandon the investment, but the jurisdiction, so Croatian companies register their holding companies in Ireland, the Netherlands or Luxembourg, and the tax base moves with them. The conclusion of the panel is therefore that lowering tax rates would not solve a problem that the rates did not create; the greatest contribution to the investment climate would come from judicial reform, i.e. the speed and predictability of resolving commercial disputes.

Speaking about investments in healthcare from the Government’s perspective, Minister of Health Irena Hrstić emphasised that the Government of the Republic of Croatia has invested around €3.4 billion in the healthcare system over the past ten years or so, and that investments continue in line with the policy of balanced regional development – from the new University Hospital Centre Osijek and the project for a new University Hospital Centre for Dalmatia, which the Ministry and the Government have already given the green light, to the hospital in Blato, whose foundation stone will soon be laid and which will be the first “Carbon Zero” hospital in Europe, heated by geothermal energy and financed by European funds. The leading principle is smart investment, with the emphasis that the goal is functional healthcare equally accessible to all parts of Croatia.

A strong diplomatic dimension was given to the Forum by the presentation of new interlocutors of the Croatian business community at the international level: Ronke Amoni Ogunsulire, World Bank Director for Croatia and Slovenia, Her Excellency Anne Toft Sørensen, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Denmark to the Republic of Croatia, and His Excellency Glenn Morrison, Ambassador of Australia to the Republic of Croatia. Their presentation opens new channels of cooperation and a direct link between the domestic business and investment community and partners outside Croatia, which is crucial for attracting investment and strengthening export opportunities. In addition to them, the Forum also gathered other esteemed ambassadors and representatives of international financial institutions, thereby confirming its role as a meeting place of the Croatian economy with international partners.

what is crane?

CRANE – the Croatian Association of Investors and Business Angels is otherwise the oldest Croatian association of investors and business angels, founded in 2008. It connects ambitious entrepreneurs with investors who invest money, knowledge, skills and business contacts in their projects, with the aim that as many innovative companies in the early stage of development as possible grow into successful business stories. CRANE is the national representative of Croatia in the European Business Angels Network (EBAN) and a member of the Global Business Angels Network (GBAN), and in addition to its investment activity systematically advocates a better regulatory and tax framework for entrepreneurs and investors in Croatia and at the level of the European Union. More at www.crane.hr.

World.title: Hybrid Electro-Diesel Train Between Split and Zagreb Now Operational
World.content:
September the 15th, 2026 – The very first hybrid electro-diesel train between Split and Zagreb is now fully operational. Here are all the details.

As of today (September the 15th, 2026) the very first electro-diesel train will enter service on the Split – Zagreb Main Station route. The train departs (as it has today) from Split station at 07:54. Poslovni reports that the new train is adapted to the specific characteristics of the Zagreb–Split line, which is partly electrified and partly non-electrified. It has 150 seats, and passengers have access to free Wi-Fi, power sockets next to the seats, a modern information system, visual and audio announcements, ramps for people with disabilities, and space for bicycles. The train also features self-service machines for buying coffee and other hot drinks, water, soft drinks, sweets and snacks.

The introduction of the new electro-diesel trains for long-distance transport continues the modernisation of the HŽ Passenger Transport fleet, while at the same time reducing energy consumption, noise and greenhouse gas emissions. Experts from the KONČAR Group, in cooperation with numerous Croatian companies, were involved in the development and production of the trains.

As part of this massive project, six electro-diesel trains are being procured, financed by a loan from the European Investment Bank amounting to 57.3 million euros. All six trains will be put into service by the end of this year. As of December 2026, with the start of the new timetable, Zagreb and Split will be connected by four daily trains, further improving the connectivity of Croatia’s two largest cities and the quality of travel.

Ahead of the first regular journey of the new train, statements for the media will be given by State Secretary for Railways Žarko Tušek from the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure, President of the Management Board of HŽ Passenger Transport Željko Ukić, President of the Management Board of KONČAR Gordan Kolak, Split-Dalmatia County Prefect Blaženko Boban, and Deputy Mayor of Split Matea Dorčić. Also present on the journey will be Zadar County Prefect Josip Bilaver and Šibenik-Knin County Prefect Paško Rakić.

World.title: Brač Fire: Residents Without Electricity Told to Follow TV and Radio
World.content:
September the 15th, 2026 – Brač residents worried for their properties and indeed their lives in the recent Milna fire were very clumsily advised to follow the TV and radio – despite having no electricity.

The Early Warning and Crisis Management System (SRUUK) was activated on Saturday evening because of a large fire in the wider Milna area on Brač. Lukrecija Zderic reports for Index that residents in that area received a message on their mobile phones with a link to instructions on how to act, along with advice to follow further announcements on television and radio. At the same time, part of Brač had no electricity, which raised the question of how exactly people without power were supposed to obtain new information about the fire.

On Saturday evening, the fire, driven by strong wind, spread rapidly towards Milna as well as the bays of Duboka and Osibova, where Resort Gava with a large number of tourists is located. More than 200 firefighters were on the ground trying to stop the fire from spreading towards the populated area.

false evacuation and sruuk activation

The red sky above Brač and Milna was visible even from Split, while Index readers filmed the firestorm approaching the settlement. As the situation became increasingly serious, various pieces of information about a possible evacuation began to arrive. Shortly before 23:00, a notice about the evacuation of the population was published on the Facebook page of the Milna Volunteer Fire Department. It stated that the situation was critical and called on citizens to make their private boats available for evacuation needs. The post was deleted about half an hour later, and services on the ground reported that there was no official evacuation.

At 23:28 the SRUUK was activated. Citizens in the endangered area received a warning via SMS or Cell Broadcast about the danger, together with a link to additional information. Clicking the link opens a page of the Ministry of the Interior (MUP), i.e. the Civil Protection Directorate, containing “Instructions for Citizens.” These are general instructions on how to behave during a fire, and below them citizens are directed to follow further announcements via television, radio and links of the Civil Protection Directorate. At that moment Milna was already without electricity. The earlier post about evacuation further confused residents. Some did not know whether they should leave the place, so they prepared for evacuation and went out onto the street by the sea.

The SRUUK activated once again that evening at 00:22, when citizens once more received a link with instructions on how to act in the event of a fire. Why residents in the endangered area without electricity were recommended to follow information via TV and radio remains unknown for now. Because of the approaching fire a partial evacuation of the most endangered parts of Milna and the surrounding area was carried out, while the entire settlement was never evacuated at any point.

a fire warning for a fire on an island was received in split… on the mainland

The Civil Protection Directorate was therefore asked for an explanation as to exactly why citizens in an area affected by a power outage were directed to television and radio, who in such a situation is responsible for delivering key information, and how many times the SRUUK was activated during the fire on Brač. We will publish the answer when we receive it. However, the problem was not only in the content of the messages. Residents we spoke to said that some received the warning around 23:00 and then again after midnight, while others received only the first message. According to their accounts, some residents of Supetar received no warning at all.

At the same time, a warning about a significant fire danger was also received by some citizens who were at that moment in Split and on the island of Hvar, even though they were not on the territory of Brač. We have also requested an answer from the Civil Protection Directorate on this issue.

a heavily criticised system

The SRUUK has previously been criticised for not being activated during crisis situations. The last time this happened was during the large fire near Omiš, in which three people died and five more are still fighting for their lives. The fire left enormous consequences — people were left without homes and jobs, thousands of hectares of forest burned, and the safety of the population remains threatened due to possible landslides.

The non-activation of the system at that time was justified by Split-Dalmatia County Prefect Blaženko Boban with the assessment that sending a warning could cause panic. On Brač the opposite question has arisen: did the unclear communication from the services further contribute to confusion and panic among residents? In the fire that has been burning on Brač for several days, around 4,000 hectares of forest, low vegetation and maquis have totally burned, as have private buildings, cars and one resort. Around 700 people were evacuated and two people were injured. There is still some smouldering on the ground, the fire has not been completely extinguished, and firefighters remain on alert.

Over 200 firefighters on the ground have for days been making superhuman efforts to defend houses and protect residents. For the locals they are heroes who risk their own lives to protect people and property. Yet the question remains how much help they receive in crisis situations from a system that the state paid 8.4 million euros for. The SRUUK was conceived as a tool for timely warning of citizens. On Brač, however, it has been shown that simply sending a message is not the end of its job, the key question is whether citizens can, after that message, actually receive clear, timely and useful information when they need it most.

World.title: Jaan Tallinn tops Äripäev rich list with €10.3bn net worth
World.content:
Tech entrepreneur Jaan Tallinn tops this year's Äripäev rich list with an estimated net worth of €10.3 billion.

There are three billionaires on the list, while all top 10 richest are men.

Tallinn, who co-founded Skype in 2003 and is now a leading figure in AI development, is joined in an unchanged top five by Wise co-founders Kristo Käärmann and Taavet Hinrikus, Bolt founder Markus Villig and media and entertainment mogul Margus Linnamäe.

Äripäev says the Top 500 as a whole also saw strong growth, with the wealth of Estonia's richest people rising by about a third on the year, to €41.4 billion.

The top 10 in the Äripäev 2026 Estonian rich list, with their net worths, are:

Jaan Tallinn (Metaplanet Holdings, Ambient Sound Investments): €10.318 billion Kristo Käärmann (Wise): €1.933 billion Taavet Hinrikus (Skaala Investments, Wise): €1.476 billion Markus Villig (Bolt): €960.8 million Margus Linnamäe (MM Grupp): €686.9 million Raul Kirjanen (AS Graanul): €559.2 million Oleg Ossinovski (Skinest Grupp): €551.1 million Anders Anderson: €497.3 million Oliver Leisalu (Bolt): €461.2 million Fjodor Berman (BLRT Grupp): €394.8 million





The first woman to appear on the list is Kristi Veeber, one of the owners of holding company Giga, who ranks 46th with €131.3 million.

Journalist: Bulk of Jaan Tallinn wealth derives from shares in Anthropic

Most of Jaan Tallinn's €10.3 billion fortune comes from AI, Äripäev journalist Ken Rohelaan said, with the businessman's stake in Anthropic — the US AI company behind the Claude chatbot — alone valued at nearly €9.8 billion.

This represented a large leap forward in his estimated net worth, Rohelaan said, telling "Terevisioon": "We already suspected a year or two ago that his wealth could be greater than what we had seen or perceived so far, but for the figure to now come in at more than €10 billion was certainly a surprise".

Tallinn got an early start on the AI boom, he noted. "His investments have mainly been focused on artificial intelligence. We may have known about AI for only a few years, but Jaan Tallinn got involved much earlier, and this early entry into the right field is essentially the main reason that helped him get this far," Rohelaan said.

Rohelaan also highlighted Berman's rise to 10th place as the year's biggest change, driven by a buyout of minority shareholders.

World.title: Auditor general: Defense scandals pose no security threat to Estonia
World.content:
Auditor General Janar Holm told ERR that the scandals that have emerged in the defense sector in recent months do not pose a security threat to Estonia. He said openly discussing problems instead makes the country stronger.

"I know many countries where it is not possible to talk about such things. This only makes us stronger," Holm said in response to a question about whether scandals in the defense sector pose a security threat to Estonia.

At the same time, Holm said the situation in the defense sector is concerning because several of the problems are systemic. He added that the more money that flows into the sector, the greater the confusion becomes.

The National Audit Office found problems with both the acceptance of goods and the awarding of contracts in 64 contracts handled by the Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK). "Wherever we looked, there was some kind of problem," Holm said. In his view, a conventional inventory is not sufficient for accounting for Estonian Defense Forces stocks and a more digital system is needed.

EDF needs accounting rules

Holm said the Estonian Defense Forces, like all other government agencies in Estonia, must begin complying with accounting rules. He said this is important, on the one hand, for the Defense Forces itself, so that it has a quick and up-to-date overview of its assets and where they are located. On the other hand, the public must be able to see whether the money allocated to the defense sector has reached its intended destination.

However, because of problems with the accounting records, a situation arose this year in which the National Audit Office went to audit the annual report and the Defense Forces and Ministry of Defense said they had €1.2 billion worth of stocks. The National Audit Office cannot confirm whether the stocks are actually worth €1.2 billion because of the problems with the accounting records. "It seems to us that the figure should be somewhat higher," Holm said.

When there is confusion, it creates fertile ground for someone with bad intentions to take something for themselves at the state's expense. Efforts are now underway to determine what assets should be there in the first place in order to establish what is missing. Holm said there is also confusion surrounding the artillery shell deal, with the information lacking a clear audit trail.

Difficult to place blame without information

When information is lacking, it is also difficult to determine who is responsible. Holm said the parties are shifting the blame back and forth. "From the National Audit Office's perspective, what matters here is something that is often regarded as bureaucracy — namely, documentation," he said.

The National Audit Office has also told the Estonian Center for Defense Investments that the information does not provide a clear audit trail.

"We are now arguing over this and classified information is also creating a great deal of confusion, but presumably there will be clarity at some point," Holm said. He said primary responsibility always lies with the agency that enters into a transaction. In this case, the main responsibility lies with the head of the Estonian Center for Defense Investments, who signed the contract.

World.title: Estonian government agrees on preliminary allocation of next period EU support
World.content:
Estonia plans to use EU funding to upgrade police aviation, strengthen border security and expand shelter capacity as part of efforts to improve the country's internal security and crisis preparedness.

The Cabinet has approved the basic framework for Estonia's national plan for the European Union's 2028-2034 budget period, including an initial proposal for allocating funding. The national plan is the central strategic document that will guide Estonia's use of funding from the EU's long-term budget.

The national plan is based on five priority pillars: the economy and competitiveness, security and resilience, rural development, agriculture and fisheries, education and social cohesion and good governance. The most important reforms and investments for the next period will be grouped under these pillars, helping Estonia achieve its long-term development goals, the government's press service said.

Under the national plan's initial allocation proposal, more than half of the funding would go toward boosting economic competitiveness and strengthening security and crisis preparedness, accounting for 33 percent and 19 percent of funding, respectively. Another 38 percent would go toward rural development objectives, including the Common Agricultural Policy, fisheries and the food sector. Education and social cohesion would receive 10 percent, while approximately 1 percent would go toward good governance.

Under the European Commission's proposal, Estonia would receive approximately €6.5 billion in the next budget period. The initial allocation through 2031 covers €5.5 billion in investment needs. The final amount of funding is still subject to change during negotiations and will depend on an agreement on the European Union's 2028-2034 long-term budget.

The final package of EU funding for the next budget period and Estonia's national plan will be completed after an agreement is reached on the EU's long-term budget and negotiations between the European Commission and Estonia on the national plan's content and funding have concluded. This is expected in fall 2027.

For example, €260 million proposed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications is intended primarily for strategic industrial investments and research and development, with the aim of establishing new production capacity, expanding factories and supporting the production of higher-value-added goods.

To modernize production, the ministry has also proposed allocating at least another €45 million to the digitalization and automation of businesses and the adoption of artificial intelligence solutions. Funding would also support stronger cybersecurity and reduced bureaucracy, helping businesses cut costs and operate more efficiently.

The proposals also emphasize the importance of ensuring that economic growth is not concentrated solely in and around Tallinn and Tartu. A total of €108 million is planned to support regional businesses and the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises outside the country's major centers. Among other things, the funding would be used to develop industrial and business areas with the aim of creating well-paying jobs across Estonia.

Helicopter procurement planned

In the field of internal security, the government plans to purchase multipurpose helicopters and a surveillance aircraft, strengthen border security, combat serious crime, manage migration and create more shelter capacity, the Ministry of the Interior said.

Police aviation capabilities need to be upgraded to ensure that Estonia can continue to provide round-the-clock border surveillance, rescue people at sea, transport patients from the islands and respond to major emergencies. The upgraded aviation capability must also make it possible to respond to several incidents simultaneously and maintain readiness when some aircraft are undergoing maintenance, being used for training or already deployed on other missions.

EU funding will also be used to strengthen surveillance of Estonia's external border. Various procedures will be digitalized to improve migration management, while digital travel documents and visas will also be introduced.

EU funding will also be used to create more shelter capacity in apartment buildings and healthcare, social services, education and cultural institutions. Public warning systems and crisis communications will also be improved to ensure people quickly receive up-to-date information and act accordingly.

World.title: Estonia rejects EU plan for mandatory EV charging infrastructure in public parking lots
World.content:
Estonia will only partially transpose a EU directive that would require half of the parking spaces outside larger stores to have the necessary cable conduits for electric vehicle charging by next year.

With Estonia's approval, the European Union updated its Energy Efficiency Directive just two and a half years ago, with one of its aims being to help promote the widespread adoption of electric vehicles.

For example, a requirement is due to take effect at the start of next year under which larger non-residential buildings would have to provide an electric vehicle charging point for every 10 parking spaces. Alternatively, every second parking space would have to be equipped with cable conduits through which the necessary cables for EV charging could be installed in the future.

Nele Peil, head of the Estonian Traders Association, said a year and a half ago that if Estonia were to meet the minimum requirements set out in the directive, installing such charging infrastructure would cost businesses between €500 million and €2 billion.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal also said at the time that if a change, such as installing cable conduits in parking lots, was not reasonable, the requirements should be renegotiated with the European Commission.

The Ministry of Climate has now decided that this provision of EU law should not be transposed, which is why it is absent from a draft law the ministry sent to stakeholders for feedback on Monday.

Ivo Jaanisoo, deputy secretary general at the Ministry of Climate, said Estonia's proposal to the European Commission is to ease the requirement to install charging points in large parking lots.

"After consulting with business organizations and looking at how technology has developed since the directive was agreed, we do not see it as possible to implement the new regulation in Estonia in this form. What is more important for promoting electric vehicles and sustainable transport in general is ensuring that the grid capacity is there in the first place, in order to support existing market practices," Jaanisoo said.

Jaanisoo said all member states are currently behind schedule in transposing the EU directive and Estonia hopes there are other countries that will also decline to transpose the requirements concerning charging infrastructure. For now, however, that remains only a hope, as it is not yet known to what extent other countries will transpose the requirements.

"Based on our discussions with other countries, we see that this may not be as high a priority or as pressing an issue elsewhere. Many countries have placed a strong priority on electric vehicle charging infrastructure and also have large numbers of electric vehicles," Jaanisoo said.

Peil said the Estonian Traders Association welcomes the Ministry of Climate's plan, although some companies have probably already begun actively complying with the directive's requirements, for example by installing cables for EV charging in their parking lots. She said those companies would also benefit if the requirement is ultimately dropped.

"Overall, this is good for them too. If the choice is between having to make this investment across 100 percent of your parking lots and bearing that cost, versus having already completed 20 percent but now avoiding the additional costs for the remaining 80 percent, then overall, it is still better than the alternative of having to do 100 percent," Peil said.

According to the Estonian Transport Administration, there are nearly 12,300 electric cars in Estonia, accounting for less than 2 percent of all passenger cars.

The Ministry of Climate is accepting stakeholder feedback on its proposed amendments to the Building Code through September 28.

World.title: Gallery: Exhibition of French photographer Jean‑Louis Courtinat opens in Tallinn
World.content:
On 15 September, the Juhan Kuus Documentary Photo Center opened an exhibition by French photographer Jean‑Louis Courtinat titled "It Concerns All of Us," featuring nearly 80 photographs ranging from his social‑documentary work of the 1980s to the present day.

For more than forty years, Courtinat has photographed people who often fall outside society's attention or toward whom we tend to avert our gaze: children undergoing cancer treatment, people nearing the end of life, caregivers and medical workers, people living in homelessness and poverty, abandoned children, prisoners, and refugees.

"This exhibition is not only about those whom society tends not to notice. It is about all of us, because vulnerability is not an exception but part of being human," said curators Kristel Aimee Laur and Toomas Järvet. "All of us have needed someone's gaze, hand, or presence. Courtinat's photos place the question before us as well: do we notice, do we look away, or do we stay? He does not ask us to pity the people in the photographs from above, but invites us to recognize in them something of ourselves and of our shared humanity. In the end, there is no 'them' and 'us' — there is only us."

Jean‑Louis Courtinat received the prestigious Prix Niépce in 1991 and, in 2025, the Visa d'or des Solidarités award for his life's work at the Visa pour l'Image festival. He took part in the major national photography commission "Radioscopie de la France," organized by France's Ministry of Culture and the Bibliothèque nationale de France. His works are held in collections including the Centre Pompidou, the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the Maison Européenne de la Photographie, and the Musée Réattu.

France's Ministry of Culture has selected the exhibition curated by the Documentary Photo Center for the official program marking the 200th anniversary of photography. It is also the only event in Estonia included in the international jubilee program.

The exhibition "It Concerns All of Us" will remain open at the Juhan Kuus Documentary Photo Center until 3 January.

World.title: Mark Gerassimenko: Why Estonia's minimum‑wage purchasing power is the lowest in the EU?
World.content:
The upcoming talks on next year's minimum wage come as Estonia faces the lowest minimum‑wage purchasing power in the European Union and one of the weakest minimum‑to‑average‑wage ratios. A year ago, the government backed away from a tripartite good‑faith agreement meant to address the problem, writes Mark Gerassimenko.

In early August, one of the most‑read articles in the business news sections of both Delfi and Postimees was the report on Estonia's low minimum‑wage purchasing power. Recent Eurostat data showed that Estonia's minimum‑wage purchasing power is the lowest in the European Union, falling just below Latvia's.

As negotiations soon begin between the Confederation of Trade Unions and the Employers' Confederation to reach an agreement on next year's minimum wage, it is worth recalling how Estonia's minimum‑wage purchasing power reached its current state.

Generally low purchasing power

Some readers reacted with disbelief: how is this possible, when Estonia's minimum wage in euros (€946 gross per month) is clearly above Latvia's (€780 per month)? The answer lies in the overview of price levels across EU countries.

Eurostat data show that Estonia's price level is by far the highest in Eastern Europe, ranking 11th among the 27 EU member states. In terms of food and non‑alcoholic beverage prices, Estonia is the sixth most expensive country in the EU.

It is therefore not surprising that actual individual consumption (which also accounts for purchasing‑power differences) is among the lowest in the EU: only Hungary, emerging from Viktor Orbán's 16‑year rule, performs worse, and Latvia's indicator matches Estonia's at 73 percent of the EU average.

Does this mean that minimum‑wage purchasing power is not worth worrying about, because overall consumer purchasing power in Estonia is weak, even though average and median earners receive more euros per month than in many Eastern EU countries? Unfortunately, that is not quite the case.

The minimum wage's ratio to the average wage is also poor

The minimum wage's ratio to both the average and median wage in Estonia is also among the lowest in the EU. While the EU's recommended target is for the minimum wage to equal about 60 percent of the median wage or 50 percent of the average wage, Estonia's figures are roughly 50 and 43 percent, respectively. Estonia and Latvia are the only EU countries where the minimum wage does not reach even half of the median wage.

This metric matters because it is not affected by purchasing‑power differences between countries: it measures how far the minimum wage lags behind the wage level typical in society. In other words, it reflects wage inequality, focusing on the lowest legal end of the wage scale.

The minimum‑wage directive adopted in 2022 states that the minimum wage must be sufficient for a decent life. As recommended benchmarks, it includes the previously mentioned targets: at least 60 percent of the median wage or 50 percent of the average wage. Unfortunately, although these figures were initially intended to be binding for member states, pressure from some countries and members of the European Parliament resulted in them becoming recommendations in the final text.

Before the most recent parliamentary elections, the Social Democrats added raising the minimum wage to the directive's recommended level to their platform. During coalition negotiations, SDE representatives publicly emphasized that without an accelerated minimum‑wage increase, no agreement could be reached on other major issues such as tax changes.

The good‑faith agreement for accelerating minimum‑wage increases

The pressure worked, and accelerated minimum‑wage increases were included in the coalition agreement. Based on that mandate, as well as trade‑union demands and the obligation to implement the directive, representatives of the government, the Confederation of Trade Unions, and the Employers' Confederation reached a good‑faith agreement in May 2023 stating that the minimum wage would gradually rise to 50 percent of the average wage by 2027.

Later, when negotiating the specific minimum‑wage levels for 2024 and 2025, the parties largely followed the good‑faith agreement. As a result, the minimum wage rose by 13.1 percent in January 2024 and by 8 percent in January 2025.

In March 2025, a change occurred that directly harmed minimum‑wage increases and the fulfillment of the good‑faith agreement. The prime minister announced a coalition restructuring, and instead of a three‑party coalition, Reform and Eesti 200 continued as a two‑party coalition.

The consequences appeared quickly. The new coalition agreement did not mention the minimum wage at all, and by late March, Minister of Economic Affairs Erkki Keldo (Reform Party) told trade unions that the government no longer considered the good‑faith agreement binding.

This decision significantly weakened trade unions' position in the 2026 minimum‑wage negotiations. The government abandoned its role as a party to the previous agreement and shifted to the role of indifferent observer.

The result? Agreement on the 2026 minimum‑wage figure was reached only by spring, the increase took effect in April instead of the usual January, and the 6.8‑percent rise was the lowest in five years, barely exceeding last year's inflation (4.8 percent). As a result, improving minimum‑wage purchasing power stalled this year, bringing us back to the starting point of the entire discussion.

To raise the minimum wage or not?

Should the good‑faith agreement to raise the minimum wage to half of the average wage be revived after the next elections? According to the University of Tartu's 2021 study on the socioeconomic impact of the minimum wage, such an increase would improve the well‑being of minimum‑wage earners and reduce both wage poverty and overall poverty indicators. The positive impact would extend not only to wage earners but also to child‑poverty indicators (report p. 92).

"In terms of food and non alcoholic beverage prices, Estonia is the sixth most expensive country in the EU."

Opponents of minimum‑wage increases often claim that they harm employment. According to the University of Tartu study, however, the impact of minimum‑wage increases on the employment probability of minimum‑wage earners was statistically significantly negative in only one year between 2010 and 2019. In several years, the impact on employment probability was statistically significantly positive (pp. 37–38). Modeling 13‑percent and 30‑percent minimum‑wage increases, the authors concluded that employment could fall by 0.2 and 0.6 percent, respectively (pp. 93–94).

A simple but telling fact also suggests that concerns about negative employment effects are exaggerated: Estonia has one of the lowest shares of workers earning near the minimum wage (up to 105 percent of the minimum wage) in the EU, staying within three percent.

Both tax‑authority data and the University of Tartu study confirm this: the number of minimum‑wage earners in Estonia has remained stable at around 20,000 people, and in 2019, about 6,000 of them worked in single‑employee companies (p. 29). These cases likely involve paying oneself a minimum wage through a company and taking the rest of the income as dividends.

Setting aside value judgments about said practice — people may have various reasons for doing it — we must acknowledge that nearly one‑third of minimum‑wage earners are effectively self‑employed, for whom paying themselves the minimum wage is a way to obtain health insurance while legally optimizing their tax burden.

According to the University of Tartu study, such single‑employee minimum‑wage companies are disproportionately concentrated in Harju County, and their most common fields are construction, wholesale, legal services, and accounting. It is unlikely that a minimum‑wage increase would cause these individuals to lose their jobs.

However, a faster minimum‑wage increase is crucial for the remaining two‑thirds of minimum‑wage earners, who currently live in official wage poverty because their monthly net income falls below the relative poverty threshold. Raising the minimum wage is an especially attractive social‑policy measure because, unlike social benefits, it does not require additional state funding; in fact, minimum‑wage increases have a net‑positive impact on the state budget. In the current fiscal situation, that is a weighty argument.

For these reasons, the good‑faith agreement for a faster minimum‑wage increase deserves to be revived, because the benefits clearly outweigh the drawbacks.

World.title: Audit: Artists' Association lacked adequate controls in fraud that caused major financial loss
World.content:
The Estonian Artists' Association has shortcomings in its administration of creative grants and artist salaries, according to an administrative‑supervision report by the Ministry of Culture, which found that control measures were insufficient, internal accounting rules outdated, and document management in need of modernization.

The Ministry of Culture reviewed how the Artists' Association has used creative grants and artist salaries this year, focusing on the case that came to light in May, when the union fell victim to extensive fraud. The goal of the audit was to establish the facts of the incident and gain an overview of how the nonprofit organization operates.

The auditors found that creative grants and artist salaries were paid to eligible recipients based on decisions and contracts, except for the fraud case, in which a total of €680,051 was transferred to accounts belonging to unknown individuals.

This year's unpaid creative grants and artist salaries will be covered by the nonprofit's own resources — through a loan secured by real estate, and through the sale of real estate and artworks.

The review revealed shortcomings in how creative grants and artist salaries are administered, and internal financial‑management controls were not sufficient. The union also lacked approved principles for paying creative grants, as required by law and its bylaws.

It also emerged that the union's internal accounting rules are outdated and do not meet legal requirements. As a result, it was possible to make bank payments without a second person's approval. In addition, information‑technology tools were not used sufficiently, allowing payments to be initiated in the bank without an accounting source document.

The audit noted that the union's document management needs modernization, its personal‑data protection practices must be improved, and its data‑protection and information‑security measures need strengthening, as they are currently inadequate.

The Ministry of Culture gave the Artists' Association until December to correct the deficiencies.

At the same time, the ministry commended the union for its crisis management and rapid implementation of changes following the fraud.

"The realized risk meant selling fixed assets, taking short‑term credit, and reorganizing key processes — changes that will continue in 2026 and beyond," the ministry stated.

The Artists' Association agreed with the findings but noted that it did have principles for paying creative grants that were lawful, though it lacked a written procedure formally approved by the council.

According to the union, it has already modernized several processes between May and August. However, it also noted that requirements related to document management, data protection, and information security are extensive for an organization funded mainly by self‑generated income and membership fees, and will require additional investment.

"We understand that as a strategic partner of the Ministry of Culture and a user of public funds, all high standards for administration and data handling apply to us. But we emphasize that, unlike state foundations, civil‑society strategic partners do not receive state support in this area," the union told the ministry.

For that reason, the union believes the ministry could support its partners, for example through training, as the fraud case highlights the administrative vulnerability of medium‑sized and small cultural institutions.

The Artists' Association is organizing a support auction to partially cover the losses caused by the fraud scheme. This Friday, an exhibition presenting the auction works will open at the ARS Art City, featuring 162 pieces. The extraordinary support auction offers a cross‑section of Estonian art. The exhibition will be open from 19 September to 7 October, and the auction will take place on 8, 9, and 10 October.

World.title: UAE’s ADNOC becomes largest buyer of Iraq’s crude in August, September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The UAE’s state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) has expanded its position as a trader by purchasing millions of barrels of discounted crude from Iraq due to supply interruptions caused by the conflict in the region.

Two sources in Iraq’s oil sector told Reuters that the UAE was the largest buyer of Iraqi crude in August and September, boosting Iraqi exports that had been severely constrained in the early months of the conflict.

ADNOC purchased 32 million Iraqi barrels in August with reductions ranging from $24.90 to $27 a barrel. In September, ADNOC purchased an additional 40 million barrels, including 10 million barrels at an $18 discount and 30 million barrels at a $25 discount.

While Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) offered ADNOC 32 million barrels in August, the UAE company only lifted 20 million barrels due to export limitations and the Basra Oil Company’s (BOC) inability to supply the required quantity.

One of the sources explained that ADNOC has shipped 14 million Iraqi barrels in September alone.

A third source said that ADNOC purchased around 20 million barrels of crude from SOMO in tenders at a discount of $25 to $27 per barrel for the September through October lifting period.

Other corporations are also purchasing Iraqi crude. SOMO discounted August-loading cargoes, attracting bidders such as PetroChina, Zhenhua Oil, TotalEnergies, Vitol, Trafigura, Mercuria, and Cathay ​Petroleum.

In August, Iran approved an Iraqi request to allow oil tankers to sail through the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad.

World.title: Anbar Health Directorate clarifies pork-breeding rumors amid recent Najaf case
World.content:
Anbar (IraqiNews.com) – The Anbar Health Directorate issued an official denial on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, firmly debunking viral social media claims alleging that its oversight teams had raided an illicit pig-breeding facility and confiscated pork intended for commercial distribution within the governorate.

In a formal statement received by Shafaq News Agency, health authorities stressed that the rumors circulating online are entirely groundless, fabricated, and completely disconnected from any inspection operations or actions executed by the directorate.

Health officials warned that amplifying such sensationalized misinformation fuels public panic and directly undermines institutional trust in state healthcare and food-safety regulators.

The directorate urged citizens, digital outlets, and news organizations to exercise journalistic due diligence by sourcing public health updates exclusively through accredited, official institutional channels while refraining from amplifying unverified social media posts.

The rumor mill in Anbar appears to have mirrored a verified, high-profile incident in Najaf governorate, where intelligence squads arrested a local butcher on Wednesday, September 9, for hunting wild boars in the marshlands of Al-Hurriya subdistrict, Kufa district, and processing the meat into minced beef products for unsuspecting consumers in central Najaf.

Judicial authorities in Najaf confirmed on Saturday that the butcher’s criminal dossier was formally referred to the Najaf Criminal Court after investigators compiled comprehensive forensic evidence, with the defendant now awaiting trial and sentencing under the provisions of the Iraqi Penal Code.

World.title: ‘You are Iraqi in any language’: PM Al Zaidi affirms pluralism in Berlin
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A candid exchange between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi and an Iraqi Kurdish journalist captured widespread attention during the Iraqi-German Business Dialogue Forum in Berlin on Tuesday, September 15, 2026.

When the journalist stood up to address the forum and apologized for not speaking Arabic professionally, Al-Zaidi interjected with a smile: “In whatever language you speak, you are Iraqi.”The gesture drew spontaneous applause across the hall, reframing a routine press exchange into a high-profile affirmation of civic identity.

The encounter resonated deeply against Iraq’s complex social tapestry, highlighting that national identity transcends linguistic or sectarian boundaries.

Iraq remains an ancient crossroads of diverse ethnicities, religions, and native languages, where Arabs, Kurds, Turkmen, Syriac-Assyrians, Yazidis, Armenians, and Shabaks form the core fabric of the nation.

The Prime Minister’s spontaneous remark served as a reminder that every citizen—whether communicating in Arabic, Kurdish, Syriac, Turkmen, or an international tongue—holds an equal, indivisible place within the Iraqi state.

World.title: Iraq signs Energy Cooperation Agreement’s fourth phase with Siemens
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz oversaw on Tuesday the signing ceremony for the fourth phase of the Energy Cooperation Agreement between the Iraqi Ministry of Electricity and Siemens.

The agreement that marks the progression into phase four of the ongoing long-term energy strategic partnership was signed as part of al-Zaidi’s trip to Europe.

The ongoing partnership aims to modernize Iraq’s power sector, build highly efficient generation capacities, and expand transmission and distribution networks throughout the country.

In August 2025, the Iraqi cabinet adopted the fundamentals of an energy cooperation strategy with Germany-based Siemens Energy.

Siemens has previously been engaged in electricity projects in Iraq, including long-term service contracts for three power plants in 2023 as part of larger energy cooperation efforts. Siemens also signed an agreement to improve Iraq’s electricity infrastructure in the same year.

Iraq relies heavily on natural gas supplies from Iran to generate electrical power and frequently experiences electricity outages. These outages worsen during the summer months when temperatures exceed 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) in different parts of the country.

To address the country’s increasing energy demand, the Iraqi government is collaborating with Siemens to develop new power plants with a total capacity of 14,000 megawatts.

The new power plants are expected to use local fuel and combined cycle technology, increasing production efficiency and lessening reliance on imported fuel.

Iraq’s electricity grid is experiencing a daily shortage of over 35,000 megawatts due to restricted fuel availability for power plants and a reduction in some external supply sources. In early August, output was barely 24,600 megawatts.

Demand in the summer fluctuates between 55,000 and 60,000 megawatts, exacerbating the supply imbalance and causing continued operational issues for the system. Production levels rely on gas supplies from Iran, which stand at around 20 million cubic meters per day.

World.title: Iraq may import LNG from French company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is exploring new avenues to secure fuel for its power plants, with the Ministry of Electricity seeking to diversify its gas sources.

The endeavor includes a preliminary agreement with a French company to discuss the supply of liquefied natural gas (LNG) and its regasification within the country in the coming phase.

The Electricity Ministry said on Monday that Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Wahib signed a preliminary agreement in Paris with TotalEnergies to supply LNG to power plants in Iraq.

The step comes as Iraq seeks to reduce its reliance on limited gas sources and secure a more stable fuel supply for its power plants, thereby increasing electricity supply hours and providing the Ministry of Electricity with additional options during upcoming negotiations with suppliers.

The agreement establishes a framework for discussions and negotiations regarding the potential delivery of LNG via a floating platform that would dock at Iraqi ports in Basra. The LNG would then be regasified and injected into the Iraqi national grid.

The agreement includes exploring the deployment of a floating platform to receive LNG shipments in Iraq and conduct regasification operations before transporting the fuel via the national gas pipeline network to power plants, according to the operational needs of the Iraqi grid.

The proposed approach seeks to enhance the flexibility of the fuel system, as LNG can serve as an additional source when necessary. This strategy also enables Iraqi authorities to evaluate the quantities, timing, and both commercial and technical terms prior to finalizing a binding agreement.

Under the initial memorandum of understanding, Iraq is continuing negotiations with the French company to finalize details regarding supplies, infrastructure, and regasification mechanisms.

This new endeavor aligns with another initiative focused on supplying LNG to the Khor Al-Zubair port in Basra. Baghdad has entered into an agreement with US-based Excelerate Energy to establish a regasification terminal that will operate independently.

World.title: ITEX IRAQ 2026 signs strategic media partnership with Al Shabab TV
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ITEX IRAQ 2026 has concluded a strategic media partnership with Al-Shabab TV, establishing an integrated broadcasting and digital coverage framework ahead of the country’s flagship information and communications technology summit.

The bilateral agreement aims to amplify the exhibition’s media reach and deliver comprehensive programming across both local and regional audiences, showcasing Iraq’s accelerating pivot toward modern digital infrastructure and public-sector technological transformation.

Scheduled to convene from September 30 to October 3, 2026, at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds, ITEX IRAQ serves as the nation’s premier convergence point for telecommunications, enterprise IT, FinTech, cybersecurity, and digital governance.

Under the newly inked arrangement, the partnership pairs the multimedia broadcast network of Al-Shabab TV with the executive convening power of ITEX IRAQ 2026, creating an expanded promotional runway for participating multinational tech vendors, domestic startups, technical forums, and public-private initiatives shaping the country’s digital economy.

The expanded media coverage framework will track core milestone events across the four-day expo, including specialized panel sessions on emerging technologies, enterprise cloud modernization, artificial intelligence integration, and high-level regulatory forums.

By broadening multi-platform coverage, both entities seek to spotlight actionable investment opportunities and homegrown technological innovations, connecting institutional decision-makers with a wider demographic of young professionals, tech entrepreneurs, and regional commercial stakeholders.

World.title: 'Meta has admitted mistake, must remove child abuse content': Govt sources say firm has no immunity
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Meta has admitted to a mistake and will immediately inform authorities about material related to child sexual abuse.

Sources said that Meta will have to remove content related to the sexual abuse of children and material that could lead people to suicide.

The government has told Meta that it can no longer be treated only as an intermediary but as a service provider, and will have to take responsibility for the content and services it provides. The development could have far-reaching consequences for Meta, sources added.

The government believes Meta may no longer be entitled to legal immunity, although the issue will ultimately have to be decided by a court, they said.

The development comes as Meta said it will report child-safety matters directly to India's National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, amid heightened government scrutiny over allegations that paid s linked to child sexual abuse material (CSAM) appeared on Instagram.

Until now, Meta primarily routed child-safety reports through the US-based National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. The new commitment will establish a direct reporting channel to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, managed by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs.





The Centre described the move as a first step and stressed that "much more" needs to be done. "Online safety of children is a fundamental principle for any social media platform to operate in India and it is non-negotiable," officials said.

World.title: Centre declares Pak-based Shahzad Bhatti Network a terrorist organisation under UAPA
World.content:
Amit Shah said the Centre has declared the Pakistan-based SBN a terrorist organisation

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday said the Centre has declared the Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN) a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).He said the decision was taken in keeping with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of adopting a zero-tolerance approach towards terrorism."The group is involved in smuggling of arms, explosives and narcotics across borders, apart from inciting youths and petty criminals into terrorism. Targeting India's democratic structure and the fabric of communal harmony, the syndicate also published hateful digital content," Shah said in a post on X.A gazette notification issued by the Union Home Ministry on Wednesday invoked Section 35(1)(a) of the UAPA to add "Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN)" to the First Schedule of the Act, which lists organisations designated as terrorist groups.The Centre said the action was taken based on its assessment that SBN was involved in "terrorism and has participated in various acts of terrorism in India.""'Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN)' is an organisation whose objective is to involve gullible youth and local criminals to smuggle arms, explosives, and narcotics from across the border, and through terrorist activities, pose a serious threat to the democratic system, communal harmony, and internal security of the country," the notification said.The notification cited criminal cases registered against alleged SBN members under laws including the UAPA, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Arms Act, Explosives Act, Information Technology Act and Prevention of Defacement of Property Act.The notification cited criminal cases against alleged SBN members under laws including the UAPA, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Arms Act, Explosives Act, Information Technology Act and Prevention of Defacement of Property Act.It said the SBN was involved in "radicalising gullible youth" through various allurements, motivating them to engage in anti-national activities and mobilising resources for such acts in collusion with other banned outfits and similarly designated entities."And whereas, the 'Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN)' is promoting terrorism through violent activities that disrupt public order and by using various digital communication platforms to disseminate provocative messages, posing a serious challenge to the integrity of the nation," the notification read.The move comes nearly a month after a coordinated operation was carried out across 14 states to disrupt the SBN terror network and thwart its plans for subversive attacks ahead of Independence Day. The operation resulted in 253 detentions and more than 200 arrests, with over 80 FIRs registered against alleged SBN operatives.The ministry of home affairs (MHA) said on August 12 that the multi-state operation was conducted in coordination with state police forces using a real-time intelligence-sharing system. The 253 detentions included 62 in Uttar Pradesh, 52 in Haryana, 51 in Delhi, 44 in Punjab, 15 in Rajasthan, eight in Maharashtra, five in Uttarakhand, three each in Karnataka, Gujarat and Bihar, and two each in Telangana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Kerala. Fresh FIRs were registered in Delhi and Karnataka.According to the MHA, SBN, described as a Pakistan-based ISI-backed terror syndicate, is linked to grenade, IED and petrol bomb attacks and targeted killings across India. The group has also been accused of paying local conduits to conduct reconnaissance of police, defence and religious sites and install CCTV cameras for espionage.Under the UAPA, inclusion in the First Schedule formally designates an organisation as "terrorist" under Indian law. With the latest addition, SBN becomes the 46th organisation on the list.

World.title: Spate of deaths: Pilots body ask govt to end exemptions to airline on their duty norms
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Following a spate of unfortunate deaths of Indian pilots on duty or duty-related activities in less than three years, the Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) has asked the aviation ministry and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to end all dispensations given to airlines from flight duty time limitation (FDTL) regulations. It has also sought an investigation into recent pilot fatalities.ââ¦deeply concerned about increasing evidence of fatigue-related operational risks; the continued deferment and dilution of certain FDTL provisions through operator-specific dispensations, and the recent pilot fatalities that have heightened concerns regarding cumulative fatigueâ¦ and pilot well-being. While FIP does not seek to establish any direct link between fatigue and the individual fatalities, these events warrant an urgent and comprehensive review of fatigue exposure, rostering practices, recovery opportunities, medical surveillance, and fatigue risk management system (FRMS) effectiveness across Indian aviation operations,â FIP president Captain C S Randhawa has said in a mail to the aviation authorities sent on Tuesday.The federation has sought âimmediate withdrawal of FDTL dispensations granted to operators in the interest of aviation safety; uniform implementation of all approved FDTL provisions; establishment of a DGCA-led national FRMS oversight programme; mandatory quarterly fatigue-reporting and FRMS performance submissions by operators; independent scientific review of pilot health trends and fatigue-related medical events and formal participation of pilot representative bodies in future FDTL and FRMS deliberations.âIn Nov 2023, an Air India pilot had died at Delhi Airport terminal 3. In Feb 2024, an Indian pilot working for Qatar Airways took ill on a Delhi-Doha flight while travelling as operating crew member and subsequently died. In April 2026, a pilot each of Air India and Akasa died. Last week, an AI pilot died in his Delhi hotel room during a layover.Big Indian airlines have managed to get multiple dispensations from FDTL norms that govern the duty hours of operating crew and their minimum rest along with the number of light landings they can safely perform. While these rules are for ensuring safety, airlines have managed dispensation by citing lack of crew that will impact their schedules.Struggling to survive in what is the most difficult period post Covid with oil prices spiking since the Iran-US war broke out this Feb and the rupee crashing amid continuing geopolitical challenges like airspace closures, airlines have so far managed to get a sympathetic view on dispensations they seek from FDTL norms. But a spate of unfortunate deaths now has alarm bells ringing in pilot circles and they want the aviation ministry/DGCA to act before more aviators lose their lives.

World.title: India-Pakistan naval ships collide in Arabian Sea: What 1991 pact says
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday said the conduct of a Pakistani naval ship that led to a collision with an Indian Navy vessel in international waters was in direct contravention of Article 10 of a 1991 bilateral agreement between the two countries.

India conveyed strong protest over the incident to Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires.

âThe Charge d'Affaires of the High Commission for the Islamic Republic of Pakistan in New Delhi was summoned to the ministry of external affairs today and a strong protest was lodged with him over the unacceptable and unprofessional conduct of Pakistani naval units at sea that led to a collision with a unit of the Indian Navy,â the ministry said in a statement.

"While the incident, which took place in international waters, did not cause any major damage, the conduct of the Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991," it added.

The ministry further said that it advised the Pakistani diplomat "to convey to the concerned Pakistani authorities the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents."





"The Charge d'Affaires of India in Islamabad has also been instructed to lodge a similar protest with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan," it said.

According to agency sources, a Pakistani naval ship came close to a frontline Indian Navy warship during a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea.

"The Pakistani vessel was travelling at high speed and manoeuvring in an âunprofessional and unsafe manner,â ANI reported quoting sources.

India-Pakistan 1991 pact: What does it say

The pact between Islamabad and Delhi was signed in April 1991 as part of a series of confidence-building measures between both countries. The measures were aimed at fostering trust and preventing accidental or unintended military confrontations.

Under the agreement, the land, naval and air forces of both countries are to avoid major exercises close to each other. If such exercises are conducted within specified areas, the main force cannot be directed towards the other side and there should be no logistical build-up close to it.

Under this pact, both nations agreed to provide notification to each other about significant military exercises, manoeuvres and troop movements near the border.

"Their Land, Naval and Air Forces will avoid holding major military manoeuvres and exercises in close proximity to each other. However if such exercises are held within distances as prescribed in this Agreement, the strategic direction of the main force being exercised will not be towards the other side, nor will any logistics build up be carried out close to it," the agreement says.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Article 10 of the agreement says that naval ships and submarines of both countries have to maintain a distance of three Nautical Miles from each other.

"The Naval ships and submarines belonging to the other country are not to close less than three Nautical Miles (NMs) from each other so as to avoid any accident while operating in international waters," it says.

Along with the 1991 agreement, New Delhi and Islamabad also committed themselves under the Memorandum of Understanding signed at Lahore on February 21, 1999, to conclude a âPrevention of Incidents at Seaâ agreement to ensure the safety of navigation by their naval vessels and aircraft.

The provision formed part of the Lahore confidence-building process and reflected the two countriesâ intention to establish arrangements to prevent accidents and dangerous encounters at sea.

World.title: Nandyal MP Byreddy Shabari says NDA government giving priority to skill development, jobs for youth
World.content:
Nandyal MP Byreddy Shabari said the NDA government was giving priority to skill development and employment security for the youth.

Ms. Shabari on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) inaugurated a conference titled ‘Assurance for the Youth’s Future’ at Sri Ramakrishna Degree College in Nandyal. Addressing the gathering of youngsters, she said lasting change, at the State or national level, was possible only through the power of the youth.

Ms. Shabari said she was happy to launch the event in her hometown, Nandyal, among the youth who would shape India’s future. Rayalaseema was once known for severe drought, farmers’ hardships and migration for want of jobs, but the situation had changed, she said. ‘Our region is racing towards development, moving away from its past struggle with drought, and the arrival of industries is completely transforming the face of Rayalaseema,‘ she said.

Chief Minister N.
